queueProgress.interpretation: Permanent research queue; BASELINE_COMPLETE is a bounded checkpoint, not global completion.

releaseHistory.releaseNotes: First executable, evidence-aware, globally expandable baseline. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.
Append-only research checkpoint: Greek Typhon/Metis, Norse genealogy/smiths, and early Chinese wuxing text layers. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Community-responsive Greek genealogy checkpoint: 16 deities/primordial figures, four Homeric Hymn subworks, comparative navigation concepts, fifty source-located claims, permanent follow-up queue and genealogy-ready graph data. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Greek primary-profile checkpoint: core deity descriptions and original names, nine Homeric Hymn subworks and sources, five newly discovered genealogy entities, Persephone abduction and Titanomachy event layers, three artifact witnesses, explicit Aphrodite origin conflict, and a permanent follow-up queue. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Mobile graph presentation hotfix: dedicated 390px SVG layout, target-relative genealogy labels, selected-entity centering, safe-area spacing, and responsive regression coverage. Mythology claims, evidence and sources are unchanged from v0.5.0. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Evidence-led thunder and storm comparison checkpoint: source-specific Thor family and Loki/Hel versus Marvel reception correction; Vedic Indra and vajra; Japanese Raijin umbrella, Takemikazuchi and eight-thunder group; Chinese Leigong and distinct Leize thunder spirit; East Slavic Perun; community-bounded Oyo Sango; Ugaritic Baalu/Haddu title and Yamm weapon cycle; extensible comparison schema and permanent discovery paths. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Egyptian solar-composite checkpoint: Amun-Ra and Ra-Horakhty separated from their component deities; Khepri and Spell 17 witness layer; Karnak Great Temple and Abu Simbel evidence; museum objects; nocturnal solar journey; Theban Triad and public Opet route; permanent follow-up discovery paths. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Eleusis evidence-layer checkpoint: Triptolemos, Eleusinian Mysteries and Great Eleusinia; Telesterion and Sacred Way; I.Eleusis 97; Great Eleusinian Relief original and Roman-copy fragments; explicit secrecy and reconstruction boundary; six permanent follow-up discovery branches. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Perses homonym audit: Titan father of Hecate, Helios-son Colchian/Tauric king, and Perseus-son Herodotean aetiological figure stored separately; genealogy, texts, restoration event, identity assessments and six discovery branches added. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Japanese thunder local dossiers: Kamo Wakeikazuchi genealogy, Kamigamo site, Kamo/Aoi festival, Kurabeuma ritual, Sotatsu screens, Fujin and explicit identity guardrails. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Ptah-Sokar-Osiris object-evidence checkpoint: Sokar and composite deity dossiers, three independent components, four Met catalogue objects, observed contents versus hypotheses, custody, provenance and permanent follow-up paths. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Ra-Atum witness-layer checkpoint: distinct Atum-Ra and Atum-Horakhty composites, Chapter 15 sun-hymn structure, Darius Susa statue cross-civilization context, rising/setting comparison guardrails and six permanent follow-up branches. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Darius statue inscription checkpoint: DSab and its three language witnesses, five-text hieroglyphic corpus, subject-peoples list, separate textual/material evidence layers and six permanent follow-up branches. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Darius statue provenance checkpoint: Susa and Darius Gate site layers, Xerxes I, separately qualified transfer and discovery events, modern custody, physical foundation evidence and six permanent follow-up branches. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Darius inscription witness checkpoint: four numbered hieroglyphic editorial segments, two twelve-unit subject-list side sets, corrected Yoyotte bibliography, DSab three-language witness structure and explicit line-collation limits.

Darius archaeological-chain checkpoint: 1972 report dossier, XSd gate inscription, official UNESCO property components, qualified Heliopolis and Wadi Hammamat links, and a transparent NMI 4112 authority gap.

Eleusis network checkpoint: two additional inscription witnesses with findspot guards, Ninnion Tablet A11036, two dated Sacred Way monuments, Telesterion phase scope and an object-preserving relief copy network.
Japanese thunder witness checkpoint: distinct Karaijin dossier, Yamashiro Fudoki Kamo fragment, dated festival phases, Kōrin A-11189-1 and a non-merging Sōtatsu-Kōrin-Hōitsu reception network.
Norse witness graph: distinct Völuspá and Gylfaginning creation triads, Ask and Embla witness nodes, Thor-Meili textual support and open Eitri-Sindri manuscript-name conflict.
Ancient Near East checkpoint: historically scoped Inana–Ištar identification, Baal title/entity distinction and parentage conflict, KTU 1.5–1.6 Baal–Mot witnesses, Anzu–Ninurta–Tablet sequence.
Chinese semantic-layer checkpoint: Hong Fan operational passage, Han Shu correlative-omen layer, Lunheng description and Mogao Caves 285/249 thunder-deity visual witnesses.
Vajra reception checkpoint: Rigveda 1.32 witness, three separately catalogued Buddhist ritual objects and a non-identity comparison network; Jain layer remains queued.

Living-tradition governance checkpoint: persistent four-level access policies for Ifá, Oyo Ṣàngó public/restricted contexts and Māori iwi/hapū variant attribution; restricted knowledge is not collected.

Explorer 2.0 checkpoint: evidence map, release timeline, witness graph, version comparison, evidence-layer filters, conflict viewer, source-quality panel, coverage heatmap, permanent-queue progress and living-tradition access-policy summary. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Story reading library checkpoint: 21 cross-civilization stories, 23 witness-specific versions, 69 readable sections, explicit claim/entity/source links, variant boundaries and living-tradition access controls.

Story maps and reading routes checkpoint: two public-procession stories, ordered story event nodes, explicit real/mythic location policy, six witness-safe thematic routes and mobile reading UI. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Original-witness comparison checkpoint: four witness profiles, seven section-level comparison topics, fourteen witness members, explicit NOT_STATED and UNMODELED states, and an Ask/Embla creator-triad conflict.

Global story-expansion checkpoint: three source-backed stories, four independent versions, twelve bilingual sections and event nodes, and a seven-target fault-isolated audit retaining queued and permission-blocked work. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Reader and offline-archive checkpoint: on-device bookmarks, per-witness section progress, accessible presentation settings, glossary/entity quick look, and self-contained bilingual HTML/JSON artifacts. No personal reading state enters SQLite, exports, or the public snapshot. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Global story expansion batch 2: Nüwa and Gonggong stories from Huainanzi and Liezi witnesses, the churning of the ocean from the Mahābhārata critical edition and the Bhāgavata Purāṇa, thirteen witness-comparison topics, two explicit witness conflicts, a textual/material witness reading route, and an eight-target audit retaining queued and permission-blocked work. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Deity stories: 26 new source-located stories (Egypt, Japan, Norse, Mexica, Maya, Sumer, China, Ireland, Slavic, Zoroastrian, Hawaiʻi) plus a public Te Ara version of the Māori common threads; build-time story cards for all 184 deities; storyteller mode and a deity-story gallery in the web app; Ogun and Olodumare remain permission-limited. Source commit stamped; database_sha256 is the pre-stamp snapshot digest.

Long-form stories: 12 retellings of 12-20 sections that follow one located public witness in order (Journey to the West, Investiture of the Gods, Theogony, Gylfaginning, Standard Babylonian Gilgamesh, Plutarch, Kojiki, Rāmāyaṇa, and long versions of the Hymn to Demeter, Baldr, Enūma eliš and Inana's Descent); deity cards carry every section of a linked story; chapter contents, next-chapter links and an on-device reading position in the web app.

claims.statement: Demeter makes the fields bear again and teaches her rites and mysteries to Triptolemus, Diocles, Eumolpus and Celeus before returning to Olympus.

claims.objectLiteral: mingles her waters with Apsû before anything was named
claims.statement: Before heaven and earth were named, Apsû and Tiamat mingle their waters, and from them are born Lahmu and Lahamu, Anshar and Kishar, Anu and Ea.

claims.objectLiteral: plots to destroy the noisy young gods
claims.statement: Disturbed by the young gods' noise, Apsû plots with his vizier Mummu to destroy them, though Tiamat objects to destroying their own offspring.
Ea puts Apsû to sleep with a pure incantation, takes his crown and aura, kills him and builds his own dwelling upon him.

claims.objectLiteral: born with four eyes, four ears and fire on his lips
claims.statement: Marduk is born to Ea and Damkina with four eyes and four ears and fiery lips; Anu gives him the four winds, with which he troubles Tiamat.

claims.objectLiteral: creates eleven monsters and gives Qingu the Tablet of Destinies
claims.statement: Urged to avenge Apsû, Tiamat brings forth eleven monsters, makes Qingu commander of her host and fastens the Tablet of Destinies on his breast.

claims.objectLiteral: agrees to fight Tiamat if the gods make his word supreme
claims.statement: After Ea and Anu both turn back from Tiamat, Marduk offers to fight her on condition that the gods make his word decree destinies.

claims.objectLiteral: has his destiny decreed by the gods at a banquet
claims.statement: At a banquet summoned by Anshar, the great gods eat, drink and then assemble to decree Marduk's destiny as their avenger.

claims.objectLiteral: makes a garment vanish and reappear by his word; proclaimed king
claims.statement: The gods test Marduk's word by having him make a garment vanish and reappear, then proclaim him king and give him sceptre, throne and weapon.
Marduk arms himself with bow, mace, lightning, a net held by the four winds, seven destructive winds, the Flood-weapon and a storm chariot drawn by four poisonous steeds.
In single combat Marduk nets Tiamat, drives the evil wind into her open mouth and shoots an arrow through her belly and heart.

claims.objectLiteral: is captured and stripped of the Tablet of Destinies
claims.statement: Captured by Marduk after Tiamat's fall, Qingu is stripped of the Tablet of Destinies, which Marduk seals and fastens on his own breast.

claims.objectLiteral: makes sky and earth from Tiamat's body and orders the stars and months
claims.statement: Marduk splits Tiamat's body like a dried fish, making the sky from one half and the earth from the other, opening the Tigris and Euphrates from her eyes and ordering stars, months and the moon.

claims.objectLiteral: creates humankind from Qingu's blood to bear the gods' toil
claims.statement: On Marduk's plan Ea creates humankind from the blood of the condemned Qingu, so that humans bear the gods' toil.

claims.objectLiteral: honoured with Babylon, Esagila and fifty names
claims.statement: The Anunnaki build Babylon and the temple Esagila for Marduk, and the gods proclaim his fifty names.

claims.objectLiteral: saw the Deep and built the wall of Uruk
claims.statement: The prologue of the Standard Babylonian epic presents Gilgamesh as the one who saw the Deep, built the wall of Uruk and recorded his labours on a stone tablet.

claims.objectLiteral: two-thirds god, oppresses the people of Uruk
claims.statement: Two-thirds god and one-third man, Gilgamesh oppresses the young men and women of Uruk until the people cry out to the gods.

claims.objectLiteral: made by Aruru from clay thrown into the wild
claims.statement: The goddess Aruru pinches off clay and throws it into the wild, making the hairy Enkidu, who lives among the gazelles and frees the trapper's prey.

claims.objectLiteral: gains human understanding through Shamhat
claims.statement: After six days and seven nights with Shamhat, Enkidu is shunned by the beasts but gains understanding, while Gilgamesh dreams of the companion who is coming.

claims.objectLiteral: wrestles Gilgamesh at the bridal door and becomes his friend
claims.statement: Civilised with bread and beer among the shepherds, Enkidu bars Gilgamesh from a bridal house in Uruk; after wrestling like bulls, the two become friends.

claims.objectLiteral: resolves to kill Humbaba to win lasting fame
claims.statement: Seeking lasting fame because human days are numbered, Gilgamesh resolves to kill Humbaba of the Cedar Forest, and Ninsun prays to Shamash for him.

claims.objectLiteral: interprets Gilgamesh's dreams on the road as favourable
claims.statement: On the road to the Cedar Forest, Enkidu interprets each of Gilgamesh's terrifying dreams as a favourable omen.

claims.objectLiteral: sends thirteen winds that pin Humbaba
claims.statement: Shamash sends thirteen winds that pin Humbaba in place, allowing Gilgamesh and Enkidu to kill him despite his pleas.

claims.objectLiteral: proposes marriage to Gilgamesh and is refused
claims.statement: Ishtar proposes marriage to Gilgamesh, who refuses her by recounting the fates of her former lovers, from Dumuzi to the gardener Ishullanu.
With Enkidu holding the Bull of Heaven by its horns, Gilgamesh drives his sword between its nape and horns and kills it.

claims.objectLiteral: is condemned by the gods, falls sick and dies after twelve days
claims.statement: The gods decree that Enkidu must die for the deaths of Humbaba and the Bull of Heaven; he curses and then blesses Shamhat, dreams of the House of Dust, and dies after twelve days.
Gilgamesh laments Enkidu, veils his face like a bride's, paces like a lioness bereft of her cubs, and commissions a statue of gold and lapis lazuli.

claims.objectLiteral: walks twelve double-hours of darkness through Mount Mashu
claims.statement: Fearing death, Gilgamesh passes the scorpion-people of Mount Mashu and walks twelve double-hours of darkness to a garden of jewelled trees.

claims.objectLiteral: crosses the Waters of Death to Uta-napishti
claims.statement: Guided by the alewife Siduri and the boatman Urshanabi, Gilgamesh crosses the Waters of Death with three hundred punting poles and reaches Uta-napishti.

claims.objectLiteral: survives the Flood and is granted eternal life
claims.statement: Uta-napishti tells how Ea warned him through a reed wall, how he built a boat and survived the six-day Flood, released a dove, a swallow and a raven, and was granted eternal life by Enlil.

claims.objectLiteral: fails the test of sleep and loses the plant of rejuvenation to a snake
claims.statement: Gilgamesh fails Uta-napishti's test of staying awake, wins the plant 'An Old Man Grows Young' from the deep, loses it to a snake, and returns to the walls of Uruk.

claims.objectLiteral: abandons seven temples and sets her mind on the netherworld
claims.statement: Inana sets her mind on the great below and abandons heaven, earth, her priestly offices and seven temples in seven cities.

claims.objectLiteral: adorns herself with seven divine powers as regalia
claims.statement: Inana takes up the seven divine powers as regalia: crown, wig, lapis beads, egg-shaped beads, pala dress, eye-paint and pectoral, gold ring and measuring rod and line.

claims.objectLiteral: is instructed to lament and seek help from Enlil, Nanna and Enki
claims.statement: Inana instructs Ninšubur to lament for her and to seek help from Enlil, then Nanna, then Enki if she does not return.

claims.objectLiteral: orders the seven gates bolted and Inana stripped as she enters
claims.statement: Told that Inana has come for her husband's funeral rites, Ereškigala orders the seven gates bolted and Inana stripped of her regalia as she enters.

claims.objectLiteral: is stripped of one item of regalia at each of the seven gates
claims.statement: At each of the seven gates one of Inana's regalia is removed, and each time she is told to be satisfied, for a divine power of the netherworld has been fulfilled.

claims.objectLiteral: turns Inana into a corpse with the look of death
claims.statement: When Inana sits on her throne, Ereškigala fixes her with the look of death, and the Anuna judges condemn her; Inana becomes a corpse hung on a hook.

claims.objectLiteral: refuses to help Inana, who craved the netherworld's powers
claims.statement: When Ninšubur pleads for Inana after three days and nights, Enlil angrily refuses, saying whoever craves the netherworld's powers must remain there; Nanna also refuses.

claims.objectLiteral: creates two rescuers from the dirt under his fingernails
claims.statement: Enki creates the kur-ĝara and the gala-tura from the dirt under his fingernails and sends them with the plant and water of life to rescue Inana.

claims.objectLiteral: is revived with the plant and water of life
claims.statement: Enki's creatures win Ereškigala's gratitude, refuse her gifts, take Inana's corpse from the hook and revive her with the plant and water of life.

claims.objectLiteral: must provide a substitute and is escorted by the galla demons
claims.statement: The Anuna let Inana ascend only if she provides a substitute, and the galla demons who know no food, drink or gifts go up with her.

claims.objectLiteral: spares Ninšubur, Šara and Lulal because they mourned for her
claims.statement: Inana refuses to hand Ninšubur, Šara or Lulal to the demons because each mourned for her in dirty garments.

claims.objectLiteral: is handed over as Inana's substitute and flees with snake's hands and feet
claims.statement: Found enthroned and unmourning, Dumuzid is given to the demons by Inana; Utu changes his hands and feet into snake's so he can escape, and the broken ending divides the year between him and his sister.

comparisons.canonicalName: Egyptian solar forms and composite deities
comparisons.descriptionEn: A source-led comparison of Ra, Atum, Khepri, Amun, Amun-Ra and Ra-Horakhty. Membership records a useful native comparison, never a global merger.
comparisons.descriptionZh: 按来源比较拉、阿图姆、凯布利、阿蒙、阿蒙-拉与拉-哈拉赫提。进入本表仅表示原生语境中可比较，不表示全局合并。

members.distinctionEn: Ra remains an independent deity even where composite expressions invoke him.
members.distinctionZh: 即使复合神名含有拉，拉仍保留独立神祇档案。
members.nativeScopeEn: Solar deity and traveller in funerary cosmology
members.nativeScopeZh: 太阳神与葬仪宇宙论中的行旅者

members.distinctionEn: No universal Atum-Ra merger is asserted.
members.distinctionZh: 不宣布阿图姆与拉在所有时期都是同一实体。
members.nativeScopeEn: Creator and solar figure in registered Spell 17 explanations
members.nativeScopeZh: 第17咒文解释层中的创造／太阳神形态

members.distinctionEn: A Spell 17 equation with Ra-Horakhty remains witness-specific.
members.distinctionZh: 与拉-哈拉赫提的认同只限特定第17咒文解释层。
members.nativeScopeEn: Becoming and rising-sun layer in funerary text and hymn evidence
members.nativeScopeZh: 葬仪文本与赞歌证据中的生成／晨日层

members.distinctionEn: Amun is not relabeled as a generic sun god in every source.
members.distinctionZh: 不会把所有阿蒙资料都改写成太阳神资料。
members.nativeScopeEn: Theban hidden/creator deity and component in Amun-Ra
members.nativeScopeZh: 底比斯隐秘／创造神及阿蒙-拉组成神

members.distinctionEn: Stored separately from Amun and Ra; component edges are not redirects.
members.distinctionZh: 与阿蒙和拉分别建档，组成关系不是重定向。
members.nativeScopeEn: Theban-solar composite with dated temple and object witnesses
members.nativeScopeZh: 具有明确神庙与器物证据的底比斯—太阳复合神

members.distinctionEn: Not every Horus form is Ra-Horakhty.
members.distinctionZh: 并非所有荷鲁斯形态都等于拉-哈拉赫提。
members.nativeScopeZh: 拉与双地平线荷鲁斯的复合表达

comparisons.methodologyEn: Every member is linked to a located claim. Textual equations, cult groupings, temple manifestations and scholarly syncretism models remain separately scoped.
comparisons.methodologyZh: 每位成员都连接已定位 Claim；文本中的认同、祭祀组合、神庙显现和学术复合模型分别保存。
comparisons.nameZh: 古埃及太阳神形态与复合神对照

comparisons.descriptionEn: A source-led comparison of thunder, lightning, storm, rain, combat and kingship layers. Membership marks a useful comparison, never identity or common origin.
comparisons.descriptionZh: 按来源比较雷、闪电、风暴、降雨、战斗与王权层。进入本表只表示“可比较”，不表示同一神、同一来源或已经证实的传播关系。

members.distinctionEn: Loki is a narrative companion/adversary, not an Old Norse brother; Thrud is Thor’s daughter.
members.distinctionZh: 洛基是叙事同伴／对手，不是古诺斯层兄弟；斯露德是索尔之女。
members.nativeScopeEn: Hammer-bearing protector and giant-opponent with thunder association in Norse textual and material layers.
members.nativeScopeZh: 古诺斯文本与物质文化层中的锤持有者、保护者和巨人对手，并具雷鸣关联。

members.distinctionEn: Greek thunderbolt genealogy and Olympian rule do not define every storm tradition.
members.distinctionZh: 希腊雷霆来源与奥林匹斯王权不能用来定义其他文明的风暴神。
members.nativeScopeEn: Thunder, lightning, thunderbolt and divine rule in specific Greek witnesses.
members.nativeScopeZh: 具体希腊文本中的雷、闪电、雷霆武器与神王层。

members.distinctionEn: Later Buddhist Sakra and ritual vajra reception remain separate from the Rigvedic witness.
members.distinctionZh: 后世帝释天与佛教法器金刚杵不得覆盖吠陀文本层。
members.nativeScopeEn: Rigvedic atmospheric, thunder/lightning, martial and water-release layers with the vajra.
members.nativeScopeZh: 《梨俱吠陀》中的大气、雷电、战斗、放水与金刚杵层。

members.distinctionEn: Not one fixed ancient personality; the Kojiki eight thunder kami remain separate records.
members.distinctionZh: 不是一位固定古典人格；《古事记》八雷神保持独立。
members.nativeScopeEn: A broad Japanese thunder-kami designation with regional and diachronic forms.
members.nativeScopeZh: 日本跨时期、跨地方的“雷神”称谓／神祇复合入口。

members.distinctionEn: Not an alias or automatic equivalent of Raijin.
members.distinctionZh: 不是 Raijin 的别名，也不自动等同。
members.nativeScopeEn: Primarily a martial heavenly envoy in classical narratives, with secondary thunder association.
members.nativeScopeZh: 古典叙事中主要是武神／天神使者，雷电为次级关联。

members.distinctionEn: Wang Chong records and rejects an image explanation; Leize’s thunder spirit stays distinct.
members.distinctionZh: 王充记录后加以反驳；雷泽雷神保持独立。
members.nativeScopeEn: Diachronic Leigong layers in classical poetry, Han criticism and later visual traditions.
members.nativeScopeZh: 古典诗歌、汉代批判记录与后世图像传统中的跨时期雷公层。

members.distinctionEn: A separate textual entity, not automatically an early name for later Leigong.
members.distinctionZh: 独立文本实体，不能自动当作后世雷公的早期名字。
members.nativeScopeEn: Unnamed dragon-bodied thunder spirit of Leize in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.
members.nativeScopeZh: 《山海经》中居于雷泽、龙身人头的无名雷神。

members.distinctionEn: No securely named medieval axe or hammer; co-invocation with Veles is not direct proof of cosmic enmity.
members.distinctionZh: 没有可靠中世纪命名斧／锤；与维列斯共同受誓言援引不等于宇宙敌对。
members.nativeScopeEn: East Slavic oath and state-cult evidence, with thunder/lightning synthesis in scholarship.
members.nativeScopeZh: 东斯拉夫誓言与国家崇拜见证；雷电领域由学术语境综合。

members.distinctionEn: Public community-backed layers only; initiated-only spaces and knowledge are not collected.
members.distinctionZh: 仅收录社群授权的公共层；入门者空间与秘密知识不采集。
members.nativeScopeEn: Thunder, lightning, justice, kingship and ancestor memory in the living Oyo Yoruba tradition.
members.nativeScopeZh: 奥约约鲁巴活态传统中的雷、闪电、正义、王权与祖先记忆。

members.distinctionEn: Baal is also a title; other Baal figures are not merged, and weapon forms remain translation-dependent.
members.distinctionZh: “Baal”亦为头衔；其他巴力不合并，武器外形保留译法差异。
members.nativeScopeEn: Ugaritic storm, rain, warrior, fertility and kingship layers in tablets and iconography.
members.nativeScopeZh: 乌加里特泥板与图像中的风暴、降雨、战士、丰饶与王权层。

comparisons.methodologyEn: Every member requires a located claim. Native scope and comparison boundaries remain explicit; umbrella figures, textual groups, living traditions and modern receptions are not flattened.
comparisons.methodologyZh: 每个成员必须连接已定位 Claim，并保留原生范围与比较边界；泛称、文本神群、活态传统和现代改编不会被压成同一套神谱。
comparisons.nameZh: 雷神、闪电与风暴神对照

conflicts.resolutionNotes: Collect manuscript readings and edition apparatus before resolution.
conflicts.summary: Eitri and Sindri may name the same smith in different textual/reference traditions, but automatic merging would erase witness differences.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Eitri is retained as the normalized-edition name for Brokkr’s smith-brother.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Sindri is preserved as a separate record for the manuscript-name problem.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep two entities until readings in GKS 2367, DG 11 and AM 242 are collated folio by folio.
conflicts.summary: Eitri and Sindri participate in a manuscript/edition naming problem for Brokkr’s smith-brother.

conflicts.claimAStatement: The Lei Xu discussion describes a strong figure striking linked drums.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Dunhuang Academy identifies a Western Wei thunder-deity image with twelve linked drums in Cave 285.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Add iconographic studies and inscriptional context before asserting transmission.
conflicts.summary: Official scholarship notes visual similarity, but similarity alone does not prove a continuous cult, workshop or textual dependency.

conflicts.claimAStatement: The operational-quality layer is derived from the registered passage.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Han correlative-omen layer is derived from the registered Han Shu witness.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain passage, date, genre and later interpretive systems separately.
conflicts.summary: Hong Fan operational descriptions and Han historiographic correlations are related but not semantically identical layers.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Modern Assyriological reference treats Inana/Ištar together while preserving the language-specific names.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The system preserves language, period and witness boundaries inside the historical identification.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain two canonical deity dossiers connected through a dated identification history.
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 伊南娜—伊什塔尔历史性对应
conflicts.summary: Historical identification does not erase Sumerian/Akkadian language, date and corpus boundaries.

conflicts.claimAStatement: RV 1.32 contains vajra terminology in its account of Indra.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Shared vocabulary and reception do not establish one physical object across centuries.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Preserve every dated museum object, textual witness and ritual interpretation as a separate record.
conflicts.subjectName: Vajra textual and material reception layers
conflicts.subjectNameZh: vajra／金刚杵文本与物质接受层
conflicts.summary: The shared term vajra links textual and material reception but does not identify one physical object.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Yuan You and Lei Xu provide early textual layers for a figure called Leigong in thunder-related imagery and escort language.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Classic of Mountains and Seas describes an unnamed thunder spirit in Leize whose belly-drumming produces thunder.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep separate canonical entities; future diachronic scholarship may add a qualified relationship without automatic identity.
conflicts.summary: The Leize thunder spirit in the Classic of Mountains and Seas and later Leigong layers share a thunder function but differ in name, form and textual setting.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Amun-Ra is registered as a syncretized expression involving Amun; the Amun entity remains independent.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Amun-Ra is registered as a syncretized expression involving Ra; the Ra entity remains independent.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep a canonical composite entity with two component edges and dated evidence.
conflicts.summary: Amun-Ra involves Amun and Ra but cannot be safely represented as a spelling alias or destructive merge.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Atum-Ra is registered as a composite expression involving Atum.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The registered hymn address combines Atum with Horakhty.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep separate composite entities and expand dated primary witnesses before considering any narrower identity claim.
conflicts.summary: Atum-Ra appears in the Persian-period Darius-statue synthesis while Atum-Horakhty appears in a sun-hymn witness; shared Atum does not establish a single interchangeable name.

conflicts.claimAStatement: One Spell 17 explanatory gloss identifies Khepri in the boat as Ra-Horakhty himself.
conflicts.claimBStatement: British Museum stela EA826 contains a twenty-one-line hymn to Khepri according to the catalogue.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Preserve both claims and forbid a global redirect pending wider witness study.
conflicts.summary: Spell 17 identifies Khepri with Ra-Horakhty in one explanation while other witnesses address Khepri independently.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Object 28.3.48 is solid rather than hollow, so no contents are inferred for it.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The separately catalogued linen-and-mud contents 21.9.1d came from inside figure 21.9.1a-c.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Never propagate one object contents to the whole type; continue object-by-object technical study.
conflicts.summary: Registered figures differ: 28.3.48 is solid, while 21.9.1a-c is hollow and preserves catalogued contents; 34.9 has only a hypothetical missing-base cavity.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Ra-Horakhty is a syncretized expression involving Ra; the Ra record remains independent.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Ra-Horakhty incorporates Horus specifically in the horizon-protector scope described by the registered catalogue.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep the composite record and explicitly state the horizon limitation.
conflicts.summary: Ra-Horakhty invokes Horus in a horizon-specific scope; a merge into the general Horus record would erase other Horus forms.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Theogony 188-206 narrates Aphrodite arising after the severed genitals of Uranus fall into the sea.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Iliad 5 describes Aphrodite falling into the lap of her mother Dione.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain the Hesiodic and Iliadic witnesses as coexisting source-level variants; do not force a single normalized parentage.
conflicts.summary: Hesiod’s Theogony narrates Aphrodite arising from the aftermath of Uranus’s castration, while the Iliad names Dione as her mother and elsewhere calls Aphrodite a daughter of Zeus.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Theogony 404-409 presents Perses and Asteria as parents of Hecate.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: No redirects or alias merges were created. Three EXPLICITLY_DISTINCT identity assessments record the source-bounded separation; additional homonyms may still be discovered.
conflicts.summary: Three major figures named Perses are now stored separately: the Titan father of Hecate, the son of Helios in Colchian/Tauric mythography, and the son of Perseus and Andromeda in Herodotus.

conflicts.resolutionNotes: Preserve separate entities; future research needs source-specific philology, shrine history and transmission evidence.
conflicts.summary: The Otokuni red-arrow Honoikazuchi and the Kojiki Yomi Honoikazuchi share a written name but occur in different witness contexts.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Kokugakuin reports that the red arrow in the fragmentary genealogy is a transformation of Honoikazuchi of Otokuni and fathers Kamo Wakeikazuchi.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The fragment identifies the red arrow as a transformation of Honoikazuchi worshipped in Otokuni District.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain separate entities and compare original-language witnesses, cult locations and transmission histories.
conflicts.summary: The Otokuni Honoikazuchi is securely attached to the Kamo fragment, but name similarity does not establish identity with the Kojiki underworld thunder being.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Kokugakuin’s Basic Terms of Shinto treats Raijin as a thunder-kami designation with multiple regional forms and rain associations.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Kojiki Yomi episode presents eight separately named thunder kami on Izanami.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Use an umbrella entity plus separate deity/group records; never force a single universal genealogy.
conflicts.summary: Raijin can function as a broad thunder-kami designation while classical and regional traditions preserve multiple distinct thunder figures.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Takemikazuchi’s name and reception support a secondary thunder association, while the registered classical actions are primarily martial and emissarial.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Kojiki traditions place Takemikazuchi in divine-generation, land-transfer and imperial-expedition narrative layers.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain martial/heavenly-envoy as primary and thunder association as medium-confidence secondary classification.
conflicts.summary: Modern thunder-god labels can obscure that Takemikazuchi’s principal classical actions are martial and emissarial.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Gylfaginning names Hel as a child of Loki and Angrboda.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Marvel’s official on-screen biography presents Hela as Thor’s half-sister in that screen continuity.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep ancient and modern entities separate and connect them only through modern_adaptations.
conflicts.summary: Old Norse witnesses make Hel a child of Loki and do not make Loki Thor’s brother; Marvel screen continuity makes Loki an adoptive brother and Hela a half-sister of Thor.

conflicts.resolutionNotes: Add archaeological miniature-axe pendants and comparative scholarship only as low-confidence, separately sourced layers.
conflicts.summary: Modern summaries often give Perun a named axe or hammer, but the registered medieval chronicle evidence does not name such a unique divine weapon.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Ugaritic textual formulae call Baal son of Dagan.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Other relational language places Baal under El’s paternity in the Ugaritic divine-family discourse.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep Dagan and El distinct; add exact KTU line witnesses before any harmonization.
conflicts.summary: Dagan-son formulae and El-paternity discourse must be compared at line and genre level.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Baal is also a lord/master title; the Ugaritic storm deity’s record therefore cannot absorb every Baal-named figure.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Louvre thunderbolt stele and Baal Cycle context support comparing Ugaritic Baalu/Haddu as a storm and lightning figure.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Never merge Baal Hammon, Baalshamin, Melqart, biblical Baalim or other regional figures by name alone.
conflicts.summary: Baal can be a lord/master title while the Ugaritic Baalu/Haddu dossier refers to a particular storm-deity figure in registered witnesses.

conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Liezi Tang Wen witness the Gonggong episode is introduced with 其後 after Nüwa's repair.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Huainanzi Tian Wen witness narrates the Gonggong collision on its own as an explanation of cosmic orientation without naming Nüwa.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep both placements. Do not adopt the later retelling in which the collision causes the repair until that reception layer is registered with exact locators.
conflicts.summary: Liezi Tang Wen places the Gonggong collision after Nüwa's repair, while Huainanzi Tian Wen narrates it as a standalone cosmological etiology without Nüwa.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Encyclopaedia Iranica reports that Xerxes brought the statue to Susa.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Encyclopaedia Iranica attributes the transfer of the statue to Xerxes I.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Treat the transfer as a sourced historical reconstruction until excavation publications or primary documentation provide a stronger chain.
conflicts.subjectName: Reconstructed Transfer of the Darius Statue to Susa
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 大流士雕像转运苏萨（学术重建）
conflicts.summary: Two database claims repeat the same scholarly attribution, but neither is a direct ancient account of the transfer route or motive.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Kyoto National Museum notes a later Hōitsu version in the reception history of Sōtatsu’s screens.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The Hōitsu work-level record is a distinct later member of the network.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Replace the work-level record with or link it to a museum object only after an official catalogue match.
conflicts.subjectName: Wind and Thunder God Screens attributed to Sakai Hōitsu — research record
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 酒井抱一《风神雷神图》版本研究档
conflicts.summary: Museum scholarship confirms a Hōitsu version, while an exact object-level holding institution and catalogue number are not yet attached.

conflicts.claimAStatement: The bronze statuette may depict Zeus if its lost attribute was a thunderbolt.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The bronze statuette may depict Poseidon if its lost attribute was a trident.
conflicts.summary: The statuette's lost attribute prevents a secure choice between Zeus and Poseidon.

conflicts.claimAStatement: DSab is inscribed on the Darius statue from Susa.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Five hieroglyphic texts accompany the cuneiform inscription on the statue.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Maintain separate corpus entities, languages and source editions.
conflicts.subjectName: Egyptian Statue of Darius I from Susa
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 苏萨出土大流士一世埃及式雕像
conflicts.summary: DSab and five hieroglyphic texts share one carrier but are not one interchangeable text.

conflicts.claimAStatement: DSab states that Darius ordered the stone statue to be made in Egypt.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The stone type supports an Egyptian provenance and is associated with Wadi Hammamat.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep textual assertion and archaeometric interpretation separate.
conflicts.subjectName: Egyptian Statue of Darius I from Susa
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 苏萨出土大流士一世埃及式雕像
conflicts.summary: The inscription states Egyptian manufacture while material analysis independently supports Egyptian stone provenance; these are converging but different evidence types.

conflicts.claimAStatement: A 2019 scholarly article cites the statue as NMI 4112.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The project retains NMI 4112 as a scholarly cited candidate until an official National Museum of Iran record is matched.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Keep the profile catalogue value noncommittal until a museum catalogue, label publication or direct institutional response confirms the identifier.
conflicts.subjectName: Egyptian Statue of Darius I from Susa
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 苏萨出土大流士一世埃及式雕像
conflicts.summary: NMI 4112 is used in specialist scholarship, while an official National Museum of Iran collection-page match remains unavailable in the checked source set.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Encyclopaedia Iranica reports the scholarly reconstruction that the statue was intended for the temple of Heliopolis.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Heliopolis is registered as a proposed original destination of the Darius statue, not as a certain excavated installation.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain as a proposed destination; collect full Yoyotte argument and competing Pithom/Heliopolis readings before stronger wording.
conflicts.subjectName: Egyptian Statue of Darius I from Susa
conflicts.subjectNameZh: 苏萨出土大流士一世埃及式雕像
conflicts.summary: The Heliopolis destination appears in scholarly synthesis but is not an excavated installation context or continuous ancient itinerary.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Völuspá 17–18 presents Óðinn, Hœnir and Lóðurr in the Ask–Embla episode.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Gylfaginning identifies the sons of Borr as Óðinn, Vili and Vé in its creation sequence.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain the poetic and prose triads as coexisting witnesses. Do not equate the differing deities without separate source-backed identity claims.
conflicts.summary: Völuspá 17–18 presents Óðinn, Hœnir and Lóðurr, while Gylfaginning 8–9 presents Óðinn, Vili and Vé in the Ask–Embla creation frame.

conflicts.claimAStatement: In the Mahābhārata critical-edition witness the tortoise king Akūpāra bears Mount Mandara during the churning.
conflicts.claimBStatement: In the Bhāgavata Purāṇa witness Viṣṇu, in the form of a giant tortoise, raises Mount Mandara on his back.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Retain both as coexisting textual witnesses. Akūpāra and Kūrma remain separate entities; no identity claim is made without an explicit source-backed identification.
conflicts.summary: The Mahābhārata critical edition (Ādiparvan 1.16) has the tortoise king Akūpāra bear Mount Mandara, while the Bhāgavata Purāṇa (8.7) has Viṣṇu himself assume a tortoise form to raise it.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Homeric Hymn 2 presents the rites as not lawfully transgressed, investigated or uttered; modern reconstruction must therefore remain evidence-limited.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Official heritage interpretation and museum scholarship identify the Telesterion as the central assembly hall for the mysteries.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Preserve public procession, building function, textual prohibitions and later interpretations as separate layers; never fill the gap by invention.
conflicts.summary: Ancient secrecy and fragmentary evidence prevent confident reconstruction of the complete inner ritual from the current public source set.

conflicts.claimAStatement: The surviving statue was discovered in the Darius Gate passage context at Susa.
conflicts.claimBStatement: The archaeological synthesis reconstructs a probable pair of statues flanking the passage.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Do not create or merge a second statue object without independent remains or catalogue evidence.
conflicts.summary: One surviving statue is archaeologically registered while the flanking pair is a probable architectural reconstruction.

conflicts.claimAStatement: Völuspá 17–18 presents Óðinn, Hœnir and Lóðurr in the Ask–Embla episode.
conflicts.claimBStatement: Gylfaginning identifies the sons of Borr as Óðinn, Vili and Vé in its creation sequence.
conflicts.resolutionNotes: Preserve both witness claims; do not equate Hœnir with Vili or Lóðurr with Vé without separate evidence.
conflicts.summary: Völuspá and Gylfaginning present different named creation triads.

因陀罗杀死了弗栗多。
因陀罗与雷相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Indra in registered Rigvedic witnesses, wielder of the vajra and linked to serpent combat, released waters, atmosphere and battle.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》中的因陀罗：金刚杵持有者，并在 1.32 与 2.12 的具体见证中与蛇敌、受阻水流、大气和战斗相连。
deityStoryCards.name: Indra

facts.textZh: 陀湿多创造了金刚杵／雷霆。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Maker of Indra’s vajra in the registered Rigveda 1.32 witness.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《梨俱吠陀》1.32 见证中为因陀罗制作金刚杵者。
deityStoryCards.name: Tvastr

facts.textZh: 特拉洛克——职掌：rain and agriculture

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Rain god linked to agriculture whose temple occupied the north side of the Templo Mayor (INAH).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与农业相关的雨神；大神庙北侧是他的神庙（墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所）。
deityStoryCards.name: Tlaloc

facts.textZh: 特斯卡特利波卡出现在“羽蛇神在图拉的衰落”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Also called Titlacauan; among the sorcerers who bring Quetzalcoatl's glory at Tollan to an end (Florentine Codex Book 3).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 又称蒂特拉卡瓦；《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷中令羽蛇神在图拉衰落的巫师之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Tezcatlipoca

facts.textZh: 科约尔沙乌基是科阿特利库埃的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Coatlicue who leads her brothers against their mother and is killed by Huitzilopochtli at Coatepec.
deityStoryCards.name: Coyolxauhqui

facts.textZh: 科约尔沙乌基是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
维齐洛波奇特利是科阿特利库埃的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Mother of Huitzilopochtli in the Coatepec account of Florentine Codex Book 3.
deityStoryCards.name: Coatlicue

facts.textZh: 维齐洛波奇特利——职掌：war; sun; patron of the Mexica
维齐洛波奇特利是科阿特利库埃的孩子。
维齐洛波奇特利在特诺奇蒂特兰大神庙受到崇拜。
维齐洛波奇特利——击败：the Centzon Huitznahua, scattered from Coatepec

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Solar war god and patron of the Mexica; born fully armed on Coatepec in Florentine Codex Book 3; his chapel stood on the south side of the Templo Mayor.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 墨西加人的太阳战神与守护神；《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷说他在蛇山全副武装地诞生；大神庙南侧是他的神殿。
deityStoryCards.name: Huitzilopochtli

facts.textZh: 羽蛇神——描述：a great wizard of Tollan
库库尔坎 · name translation of · 羽蛇神

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Great wizard of Tollan whose glory ends when sorcerers come to him in Florentine Codex Book 3.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷中图拉的大法师，巫师们到来后他的荣光走向终结。
deityStoryCards.name: Quetzalcoatl

facts.textZh: 佩蕾——职掌：volcanoes; elemental force; creator of volcanic landscapes

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Hawaiian volcano deity who, in NPS's summary of oral history, voyaged from Kahiki and made her home in Halemaʻumaʻu crater at Kīlauea.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 夏威夷火山之神；据美国国家公园管理局对口述传统的概述，她从卡希基远航而来，定居基拉韦厄的哈雷茂茂火山口。
deityStoryCards.name: Pele

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Wise god who slays Apsû, fathers Marduk and creates humankind from Kingu's blood in Enūma eliš; the Akkadian name associated with Sumerian Enki, kept as a separate entity.
deityStoryCards.name: Ea (Nudimmud)

facts.textZh: 马尔杜克击败了提亚马特。
提亚马特出现在“马尔杜克与提亚马特之战”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Tiamat's champion, given the Tablet of Destinies; after his defeat humankind is made from his blood (Enūma eliš IV, VI).
deityStoryCards.name: Qingu

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Primordial fresh water, begetter of the gods with Tiamat in Enūma eliš, slain by Ea.
deityStoryCards.name: Apsû

facts.textZh: 马尔杜克使用马尔杜克之弓。
马尔杜克使用马尔杜克之网。
马尔杜克击败了提亚马特。
马尔杜克出现在“马尔杜克与提亚马特之战”之中。
佩伦与维列斯一同被呼告。
佩伦与980 年基辅山岗神像相关。
佩伦出现在往年纪事中。
佩伦与雷相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Perun in East Slavic chronicle witnesses: treaty oaths, the 980 Kyiv idol and its 988 removal are separate claims; no unsupported universal pantheon or named weapon is asserted.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《往年纪事》所见东斯拉夫佩伦：条约誓言、980 年基辅神像与 988 年毁像分别登记；“全斯拉夫唯一主神”与命名神器不作无证断言。
deityStoryCards.name: Perun

beats.textZh: 佩伦与维列斯一同被呼告。

facts.textZh: 莫科什与980 年基辅山岗神像相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Named last among the idols Volodimer set up on the Kyiv hill in the Primary Chronicle's annal for 980; no function is stated there.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条中弗拉基米尔在基辅山岗所立神像名单的最后一位；该处未说明其职能。
deityStoryCards.name: Mokosh

facts.textZh: 天照大神是伊邪那岐的孩子。
须佐之男是伊邪那岐的孩子。
伊邪那岐与伊邪那美是配偶。
伊邪那岐出现在“淤能碁吕岛的形成”之中。
伊邪那岐出现在“伊邪那岐的禊祓”之中。
伊邪那岐——情节：divides the realms among his three noble children

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Male creator deity of the Kojiki: with Izanami he forms Onogoro Island, follows her to Yomi, and on returning gives birth to Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi and Susanoo as he purifies himself.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》中的男性创世神：与伊邪那美造出淤能碁吕岛，追往黄泉，归来禊祓时生出天照大神、月读与须佐之男。
deityStoryCards.name: Izanagi

facts.textZh: 火之迦具土神是伊邪那美的孩子。
伊邪那岐与伊邪那美是配偶。
伊邪那美出现在“淤能碁吕岛的形成”之中。
伊邪那美出现在“伊邪那岐追往黄泉”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Female creator deity of the Kojiki: with Izanagi she forms the land, dies after giving birth to the fire deity, and remains in Yomi.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》中的女性创世神：与伊邪那岐一同造地，生火神后被灼伤而死，留在黄泉。
deityStoryCards.name: Izanami

facts.textZh: 伏雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Fusuikazuchi

beats.textZh: 加雷神／地方雷神——关联：must not be merged with Kamo Wakeikazuchi solely because both are thunder kami
加雷神／地方雷神与雷神相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Name used for thunder kami at local shrines in the Kokugakuin overview; distinct from the generic Raijin dossier and Kamo Wakeikazuchi.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 國學院资料列为地方神社所奉雷神名之一；本档与 Raijin 泛称及贺茂别雷大神分开。
deityStoryCards.name: Karaijin

facts.textZh: 土雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Tsuchiikazuchi

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Food goddess killed by Susanoo after his expulsion; silkworms, rice, millet, beans and barley grow from her body (Kojiki, Sect. XVII).
deityStoryCards.name: Ōgetsuhime

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Ooikazuchi

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Kami whose possessed dance before the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling makes the eight hundred myriad deities laugh and draws Amaterasu out (Kojiki, Sect. XVI).
deityStoryCards.name: Ame-no-Uzume

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Kami of great strength who hides beside the door of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling and draws Amaterasu out by the hand (Kojiki, Sect. XVI).
deityStoryCards.name: Ame-no-Tajikarao

facts.textZh: 天照大神是伊邪那岐的孩子。
草薙剑 · presented to · 天照大神

beats.textZh: 建御雷出现在古事记中。
建御雷与雷相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Primarily a martial heavenly envoy in registered classical narratives; thunder association remains secondary and does not merge the deity with Raijin.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 古典叙事主要登记为武神／天神使者；雷电关联为次级且不与“雷神”自动合并。
deityStoryCards.name: Takemikazuchi

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Child of Takami-musubi whom the assembled deities ask to devise the plan that brings Amaterasu out of the Heavenly Rock-Dwelling (Kojiki, Sect. XVI).
deityStoryCards.name: Omoikane

facts.textZh: 月读——称号：Moon-Night-Possessor (Chamberlain's rendering)

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Moon deity born when Izanagi washes his right eye (Kojiki); Chamberlain renders the name 'Moon-Night-Possessor'.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 月神；《古事记》中伊邪那岐洗右眼时所生，张伯伦译作“掌管月夜者”。
deityStoryCards.name: Tsukuyomi

facts.textZh: 析雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Sakuikazuchi

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Youngest daughter of Ashinazuchi and Tenazuchi in Izumo, saved from the eight-forked serpent by Susanoo, who becomes her husband (Kojiki, Sect. XVIII–XIX).
deityStoryCards.name: Kushinadahime

facts.textZh: 火之迦具土神是伊邪那美的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Fire deity whose birth burns Izanami in the Kojiki; Chamberlain calls him the Deity-of-Fire and names him Kagu-tsu-chi in his notes.
deityStoryCards.name: Kagutsuchi (Deity of Fire)

facts.textZh: 火雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Honoikazuchi

facts.textZh: 火雷神（乙训传统）是贺茂别雷大神的父母。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Honoikazuchi of the Otokuni red-arrow genealogy; not automatically merged with the Kojiki Yomi thunder kami.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 学术条目所述乙训郡火雷神／红箭谱系人物；不与《古事记》黄泉八雷中的火雷自动合并。
deityStoryCards.name: Honoikazuchi (Otokuni tradition)

facts.textZh: 贺茂建角身命是玉依姬（贺茂传统）的父母。
《山城国风土记》贺茂残片提到玉依姬（贺茂传统）。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Kamo-genealogy Tamayorihime; the title/name can denote other figures, so this record is scoped.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 贺茂谱系中的玉依姬；“玉依姬”也可指其他人物，因此使用限定实体。
deityStoryCards.name: Tamayorihime (Kamo tradition)

facts.textZh: 若雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode; detailed form and character remain uncertain.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一；具体形态和性格仍不确定。
deityStoryCards.name: Wakaikazuchi

facts.textZh: 火雷神（乙训传统）是贺茂别雷大神的父母。
贺茂别雷大神在贺茂别雷神社（上贺茂神社）受到崇拜。
贺茂祭（葵祭）与贺茂别雷大神相关。
贺茂别雷大神与雷神相关。
贺茂别雷大神与雷相关。
贺茂竞马仪式与贺茂别雷大神相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Enshrined deity of Kamigamo Jinja; local genealogy, shrine tradition and the broader Raijin umbrella remain separate.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 贺茂别雷神社主祭神；地方谱系、神社传承与雷神总称层分别保存。
deityStoryCards.name: Kamo Wakeikazuchi no Okami

facts.textZh: 贺茂建角身命是玉依姬（贺茂传统）的父母。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Father of Tamayorihime and maternal grandfather of Kamo Wakeikazuchi in the fragmentary genealogy.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 贺茂谱系中玉依姬之父、贺茂别雷之母系祖父。
deityStoryCards.name: Kamo Taketsunumi no Mikoto

beats.textZh: 贺茂别雷大神与雷神相关。
俵屋宗达《风神雷神图屏风》描绘了雷神。
加雷神／地方雷神与雷神相关。
尾形光琳《风神雷神图屏风》A-11189-1描绘了雷神。
雷神——关联：serpent or child manifestation motifs in some local traditions
雷神——关联：rain production in some local traditions

facts.textZh: 雷神与雷相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Umbrella entry for Japanese thunder-kami traditions; regional deities and the Kojiki eight thunder kami remain distinct.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: “雷神”作为跨时期的雷神称谓／复合入口；地方雷神与古典八雷分别保存。
deityStoryCards.name: Raijin

facts.textZh: 须佐之男是伊邪那岐的孩子。
须佐之男击败了八岐大蛇。
须佐之男出现在“从八岐大蛇体内发现草薙剑”之中。

beats.textZh: 俵屋宗达《风神雷神图屏风》描绘了风神。
尾形光琳《风神雷神图屏风》A-11189-1描绘了风神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Japanese wind-deity entry currently limited to the later Sotatsu screen witness.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 日本风神入口；本批仅登记宗达屏风中的后世图像见证。
deityStoryCards.name: Fujin

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the Kojiki eight thunder kami; identity with later similarly named shrine traditions is unknown.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一；与后世同名神社传统的关系未知。
deityStoryCards.name: Naruikazuchi

facts.textZh: 黑雷属于《古事记》八雷神。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: One of the eight thunder kami in the Kojiki Yomi episode.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《古事记》黄泉段八雷神之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Kuroikazuchi

facts.textZh: 塔内是兰吉努伊的孩子。
塔加罗阿是兰吉努伊的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sky father who, with Papatūānuku, emerges from darkness; their children separate them and let in the light (Te Ara).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 天父；与帕帕图阿努库从黑暗中出现，孩子们把他们分开，光明由此进入世界（Te Ara）。
deityStoryCards.name: Ranginui

facts.textZh: 塔内是帕帕图阿努库的孩子。
塔加罗阿是帕帕图阿努库的孩子。
帕帕图阿努库出现在“兰吉努伊与帕帕图阿努库的分离”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Earth mother joined to Ranginui until their children part them (Te Ara's summary of common threads).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 地母；与兰吉努伊相连，直到孩子们把他们分开（Te Ara 对共同线索的概述）。
deityStoryCards.name: Papatūānuku

facts.textZh: 塔内是帕帕图阿努库的孩子。
塔内是兰吉努伊的孩子。
塔内出现在“兰吉努伊与帕帕图阿努库的分离”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Named by Te Ara as atua of the forests; in some tribal versions important in separating earth and sky.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: Te Ara 所说的森林之神；在部分部族版本中是分开天地的重要角色。
deityStoryCards.name: Tāne

facts.textZh: 塔加罗阿——职掌：sea
塔加罗阿是帕帕图阿努库的孩子。
塔加罗阿是兰吉努伊的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Named by Te Ara as atua of the sea, one of the children of Ranginui and Papatūānuku.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: Te Ara 所说的海洋之神，兰吉努伊与帕帕图阿努库的孩子之一。
deityStoryCards.name: Tangaroa

facts.textZh: 布里吉德是达格达的孩子。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Bríg, daughter of the Dagda in Cath Maige Tuired, whose keening for her son Rúadán is the first heard in Ireland.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《第二次马格图雷德之战》中达格达之女布里格，为儿子鲁阿丹哀哭，是爱尔兰第一次听到的哀歌。
deityStoryCards.name: Brigid

facts.textZh: 莫莉甘出现在“第二次马格图雷德之战”之中。
莫莉甘——情节：promises to take Indech's heart's blood and the kidneys of his valour

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Daughter of Ernmas who meets the Dagda at Samain, promises Indech's death and proclaims the victory after the second battle of Mag Tuired.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 恩玛斯之女；萨温节与达格达相会，许诺击杀因德赫，并在第二次马格图雷德之战后宣告胜利。
deityStoryCards.name: The Morrígan

facts.textZh: 布里吉德是达格达的孩子。
达格达出现在“第二次马格图雷德之战”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: In Cath Maige Tuired, owner of a cauldron from which no company left unsatisfied; meets the Morrígan at the Unshin before the battle.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《第二次马格图雷德之战》中拥有“无人离去不饱足”之大锅的神；战前在乌恩辛河边与莫莉甘相会。
deityStoryCards.name: The Dagda

facts.textZh: 鲁格出现在“第二次马格图雷德之战”之中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: The Samildánach, master of all arts, who in Cath Maige Tuired kills Balor with a sling stone.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: “百艺之主”，在《第二次马格图雷德之战》中用投石击杀巴洛尔。
deityStoryCards.name: Lugh

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Aged celestial god Itzamnaaj with an avian avatar, important in Maya primordial myths (Met, 2022).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 年老的天神伊察姆纳（Itzamnaaj），有一个鸟形化身，在玛雅太初神话中地位重要（大都会博物馆，2022）。
deityStoryCards.name: Itzamna

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Feathered-serpent name linked to El Castillo, the 'Temple of Kukulkan' at Chichen-Itza; UNESCO reports it as the Maya rendering of a Tula ruler's Quetzalcoatl name.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 与奇琴伊察“库库尔坎神庙”相连的羽蛇之名；联合国教科文组织称其为图拉统治者“羽蛇”名号的玛雅译名（通行说法）。
deityStoryCards.name: Kukulkan

facts.textZh: 恰克——职掌：rain

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Maya rain god, written Chahk in Classic hieroglyphs; shown waist-deep in water on a Met plate.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 玛雅雨神，古典期象形文字写作 Chahk；大都会博物馆的陶盘上他半身浸在水中。
deityStoryCards.name: Chaac

facts.textZh: 安格拉·曼纽与阿胡拉·马兹达为敌。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: In Videvdad 1, 'all death', who answers each good land made by Ahura Mazda with a counter-created plague.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《万迪达德》第一章中“全然是死亡”的存在，对阿胡拉·马兹达创造的每一片良地施以反创造的灾祸。
deityStoryCards.name: Angra Mainyu

facts.textZh: 密特拉——称号：lord of wide pastures

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Lord of wide pastures in the Mihr Yasht: created by Ahura Mazda as worthy of worship as himself, guardian of the contract, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 《密赫尔颂》中的“广阔牧场之主”：阿胡拉·马兹达所造、与其同受崇拜，守护契约，有千耳万眼。
deityStoryCards.name: Mithra

facts.textZh: 安格拉·曼纽与阿胡拉·马兹达为敌。
DSab 三语楔形文字铭文提到阿胡拉·马兹达。

尚戈与尚戈双斧祭仪杖相关。
尚戈与雷相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sango in the living Oyo Yoruba tradition, with public thunder, justice, kingship and ancestor-memory layers; restricted knowledge is represented only by access metadata.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 奥约约鲁巴活态传统中的 Ṣàngó：雷、闪电、正义、王权与祖先记忆公共层；受限知识只登记访问边界，不收集秘密内容。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Sun god whom Gilgameš asks for help; he grants warriors to guide the expedition against Ḫuwawa (ETCSL 1.8.1.5).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 太阳神；吉尔伽美什向他求助，他赐下勇士为远征胡瓦瓦引路（ETCSL 1.8.1.5）。
deityStoryCards.name: Utu

facts.textZh: 伊南娜—伊什塔尔历史性对应包括伊南娜。
伊南娜出现在伊南娜下冥界中。
伊南娜出现在“伊南娜下冥界事件”之中。
伊南娜 · historically identified with · 伊什塔尔

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Moon god who sails with gifts to Nibru, the city of his father Enlil, and returns with blessings for Urim (ETCSL 1.5.1).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 月神；带着礼物乘船前往父亲恩利尔的城市尼普尔，带回给乌尔的祝福（ETCSL 1.5.1）。
deityStoryCards.name: Nanna

facts.textZh: 埃列什基伽勒出现在伊南娜下冥界中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Goddess who curses Enki after he eats the plants of Dilmun and later brings forth deities to heal him (ETCSL 1.1.1).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 恩基吃下迪尔蒙的植物后诅咒他、之后又生出众神为他治病的女神（ETCSL 1.1.1）。
deityStoryCards.name: Ninhursag

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Inana's minister, who laments for her and seeks help from Enlil, Nanna and Enki in Inana's Descent.
deityStoryCards.name: Ninšubur

beats.textZh: 安——职掌：heaven
安与恩基相关。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Senior god of heaven; Enki and the World Order praises Enki as beloved of holy An (ETCSL 1.1.3).
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 天上的老一辈神；《恩基与世界秩序》称恩基为“神圣的安所钟爱者”（ETCSL 1.1.3）。
deityStoryCards.name: An

facts.textZh: 恩利尔拥有命运泥板。
恩利尔——情节：refuses to help Inana, who craved the netherworld's powers
恩基见于恩基与世界秩序。
安与恩基相关。
恩基出现在“恩基的病与宁胡尔萨格的救治”之中。
宁胡尔萨格治愈了恩基。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Inana's husband, handed to the demons as her substitute in Inana's Descent.
deityStoryCards.name: Dumuzid

facts.textZh: 伊南娜—伊什塔尔历史性对应包括伊什塔尔。
伊南娜 · historically identified with · 伊什塔尔

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Akkadian sun god who protects Gilgamesh and sends thirteen winds against Humbaba; the Akkadian counterpart of Sumerian Utu, kept as a separate entity.
deityStoryCards.name: Shamash

facts.textZh: 阿卡德《安祖神话》中的宁努尔塔出现在安祖神话中。

deityStoryCards.hookEn: Dossier scoped to Ninurta’s role in the Akkadian Anzu myth.
deityStoryCards.hookZh: 本档聚焦《安祖神话》中击败安祖并收回命运泥板的角色。
deityStoryCards.name: Ninurta in the Akkadian Anzu myth
deityStoryCards.nameZh: 阿卡德《安祖神话》中的宁努尔塔

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: place_profiles latitude/longitude joined to canonical entities
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Only real places with explicit coordinates and a non-baseline evidence grade are plotted; missing coordinates are not inferred.
explorerFeatures.notes: The initial coordinate-backed layer is intentionally sparse.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: stories, story_versions, story_sections, story_claim_links, story_entity_links and source metadata
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Every section is an independent summary scoped to a named witness; gaps and variants remain visible.
explorerFeatures.notes: Initial cross-civilization reading release with 21 stories and 23 witness versions.

explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: The timeline dates database releases; free-text mythic periods are not forced onto a modern absolute chronology.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: claims, evidence and sources connected to canonical entities
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: A graph edge means an explicit database link, not common origin or identity.
Release metadata comparison does not imply that historical coverage is complete.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: claims assertion_scope, knowledge_layer, review_status and evidence evidence_type
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Filters expose recorded labels; they do not upgrade uncertain evidence.
Open and resolved-as-variants records remain visible; no forced single answer is produced.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: sources evidence_tier, verification_status, source_type and rights_status
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Counts describe registered source metadata, not a universal ranking of traditions.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: canonical entities, claims, evidence, conflicts and civilization membership
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Coverage is a research-density indicator, never a completeness score or measure of cultural importance.
BASELINE_COMPLETE marks a bounded target checkpoint, not an all-complete tradition.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: tradition_access_policies access levels and public governance scope
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Public visibility never grants permission to collect restricted or initiatory knowledge.
Alignment is editorial navigation. NOT_STATED and UNMODELED are explicit gaps, not negative claims.
explorerFeatures.notes: First batch covers Aphrodite origins and Ask/Embla creator triads.

explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Target failures and permission blocks remain visible and do not imply failure or completion for another tradition.
explorerFeatures.notes: The sealed checkpoint contains Maya, Japanese and Khmer stories; China and India remain queued, while Māori and Yorùbá are permission-gated.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: Versioned browser localStorage containing bookmarks, section progress and presentation settings only.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Local state is not evidence and never enters SQLite, JSONL, CSV or the public snapshot.
explorerFeatures.notes: Sealed on-device reader tools use a versioned localStorage key; no account, telemetry or cloud synchronization is introduced.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: Generated from the same browser-safe story snapshot used by the public explorer.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: The archive preserves source, locator, evidence-note and rights boundaries; it does not reproduce evidence short quotes.
explorerFeatures.notes: Sealed self-contained HTML and JSON remain searchable, bilingual and print-friendly while preserving source and rights boundaries.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: All rows of story_expansion_batches with their targets, newest first.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Earlier sealed batches stay unchanged; a later batch can complete a target that an earlier batch recorded as queued.
explorerFeatures.notes: Sealed: the story library switches between the sealed v0.28 and v0.30 batch audits, newest first.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: Build-time cards for every deity-classified entity: linked story versions, evidence-backed claim beats and access policies.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: A card never adds facts: each beat is an existing claim with evidence, and permission-limited deities show their boundary instead of a story.
explorerFeatures.notes: Sealed: 184 deity cards — 111 linked to full stories, 71 evidence cards, 2 permission-limited.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: Full-screen, one-beat-at-a-time presentation of story sections and deity-card beats from the public snapshot.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Source notes and uncertainty notes stay one tap away on every beat.
explorerFeatures.notes: Keyboard, swipe and on-screen controls; preferences stay on the device.

explorerFeatures.dataBasis: Story versions of 12-20 sections that retell one located witness in order; deity cards show every section of a linked story.
explorerFeatures.evidenceCaveat: Each section is anchored to its own claim with evidence at the same locator; omitted passages are named, not filled in.
explorerFeatures.notes: Sealed: 12 long-form stories (173 sections) — 8 new stories and long versions of 4 existing ones; 60 deity cards open on a long story.

Quick-look terms are derived at render time from the public story snapshot.
Only story IDs are stored in the browser-local versioned state key.

readingRoutes.descriptionEn: Compare how distinct texts and communities narrate beginnings without combining them into one creation history.
readingRoutes.descriptionZh: 比较不同文本与社群如何叙述世界或人类的开始，不拼成单一创世史。
readingRoutes.evidencePolicy: Keep every witness and community scope separate; no universal synthesis.
