stories.canonicalTitle: Frigg's oaths and the death of Baldr
stories.editorialNote: 依据《欺骗古鲁菲》第20、49章；之后的冥界求情与报复情节尚未逐段登记。
stories.summaryEn: Frigg, Odin's wife, knows all fates. When her son Baldr dreams of danger, she makes fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts swear not to harm him — all except a young shoot of mistletoe. In the end it is mistletoe that kills Baldr.
stories.summaryZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子，知道一切命运。她的儿子巴德尔梦见自己有危险，她便让火、水、金属、石头、草木和野兽都发誓不伤害他——唯独漏掉了一株幼小的槲寄生。巴德尔最后正是被槲寄生杀死的。
stories.titleZh: 弗丽嘉的誓言与巴德尔之死

claims.statement: Baldr dreams ominous dreams threatening his life, and the Æsir resolve to secure protection for him against every danger.
Frigg takes oaths from fire, water, metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poisons and snakes not to harm Baldr.
Disguised as a woman, Loki learns from Frigg that the young mistletoe west of Valhöll swore no oath, and pulls it up.
Guided by Loki, the blind Höðr throws the mistletoe, which pierces Baldr and kills him.
Odin bears Baldr's death most heavily of all the gods, understanding best what a loss it is for the Æsir.
At Frigg's request Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, mounts Sleipnir and rides to Hel to ransom Baldr.
At Baldr's ship-funeral his wife Nanna dies of grief and is burned beside him, while Odin lays the ring Draupnir on the pyre.
Hermóðr rides nine nights through dark valleys to the Gjallarbrú, where the maiden Móðguðr tells him the road to Hel lies downward and north.
Hel agrees to release Baldr only if all things in the world, living and dead, weep for him; if any refuses, he stays.
The Æsir send messengers through the world, and men, beasts, earth, stones, trees and metals all weep for Baldr.
A giantess named Þökk, believed to be Loki, alone refuses to weep for Baldr, so he remains in Hel.
When Loki, as a salmon, tries to leap over the gods' net in the Fránangr falls, Thor catches him by the tail.
With Loki bound by his son's entrails beneath Skaði's serpent, Sigyn holds a bowl to catch the venom; when she empties it, his writhing causes earthquakes.

events.summaryEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow.
events.summaryZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。

events.summaryEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes.
events.summaryZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。

events.summaryEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm.
events.summaryZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。

events.summaryEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind.
events.summaryZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。

events.summaryEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him.
events.summaryZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。

events.summaryEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr.
events.summaryZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？

events.summaryEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea.
events.summaryZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。

events.summaryEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。

events.summaryEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。

events.summaryEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard.
events.summaryZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。

events.summaryEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk.
events.summaryZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。
events.titleEn: The giantess who would not weep
events.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

events.summaryEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls.
events.summaryZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。

events.summaryEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each.
events.summaryZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。

versions.narrativeScope: 不祥的梦、万物的誓言、槲寄生、葬礼、赫尔莫德下冥界、万物哭泣与洛基受罚
versions.rightsNote: 古诺斯语原文属公共领域；现代译本受版权保护，本站只发布章节定位与独立讲述。

sections.bodyEn: Baldr, Odin's son, is the best of the gods and all praise him; so fair and bright that the whitest flower is called Baldr's brow. He is the wisest, most eloquent and most merciful of the Æsir, though none of his judgements can be fulfilled. Then Baldr dreamed great and perilous dreams threatening his life, and when he told the Æsir they took counsel together and resolved to ask protection for him from every kind of danger.
sections.bodyZh: 奥丁的儿子巴德尔是众神中最好的一位，人人都称赞他。他容貌俊美、光彩照人，有一种最白的花就因为像他的睫毛那样白，被人们称作“巴德尔的睫毛”。他是阿萨神族中最聪明、最善于言辞、最仁慈的神，可是他的判决却从来不能实现。这一天，巴德尔做了几个可怕的梦，梦见自己的性命将要遭到危险。他把这些梦告诉了阿萨众神，众神聚在一起商议，最后决定：要为巴德尔求得一切东西的保护，使他免受任何伤害。

sections.bodyEn: Frigg took oaths that they would not harm Baldr from fire and water, iron and every metal, stones, the earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds, poison and snakes. When this was done it became a sport of the Æsir: Baldr would stand in the assembly while some shot at him, some struck at him and some threw stones, and nothing harmed him. They all thought it a great honour.
sections.bodyZh: 于是弗丽嘉出发，让世间万物都立下誓言，不伤害巴德尔：火与水、铁和各种金属、石头、泥土、树木、疾病、走兽、飞鸟、毒物和蛇，全都发了誓。这件事办成之后，众神都放下心来，并且以此为乐：巴德尔站在集会的场地中央，其他的神有的向他射箭，有的用刀剑砍他，有的向他扔石头，可是无论做什么都伤不了他。众神都认为这是一件了不起的荣耀。

sections.bodyEn: Loki Laufeyjarson was displeased that Baldr took no harm. He went to Frigg at Fensalir in the likeness of a woman. Frigg told the stranger that neither weapons nor trees would harm Baldr, for she had taken oaths of all things. Had everything sworn? asked the woman. Frigg answered that a young shoot grew west of Valhöll called mistletoe, which seemed too young to ask for an oath. The woman went away; Loki took the mistletoe, pulled it up and went to the assembly.
sections.bodyZh: 劳菲之子洛基看见这一切，心里很不高兴，因为巴德尔毫发无伤。他变成一个女人，来到弗丽嘉住的芬萨利尔宫。弗丽嘉问这位女子：你知道阿萨众神在集会上做什么吗？女人说：他们都在朝巴德尔射箭、扔东西，可是什么也伤不了他。弗丽嘉说：不论是兵器还是木头，都伤不了巴德尔，因为我已经让万物都立了誓。女人问：真的万物都向你发誓不伤害巴德尔了吗？弗丽嘉答道：在瓦尔哈拉的西边，长着一棵小小的树苗，叫作槲寄生。我觉得它太年幼了，就没有让它发誓。那女人听了便走了。洛基找到槲寄生，把它拔下来，带到集会的地方去。

sections.bodyEn: Höðr stood at the edge of the ring, for he was blind. Loki asked why he did not shoot at Baldr. Because I cannot see where he is, said Höðr, and I have no weapon. Loki said he should honour Baldr like the others, and offered to show him where Baldr stood. Höðr took the mistletoe and threw it as Loki directed; it pierced Baldr and he fell dead to the earth. It was, says Snorri, the greatest misfortune ever to befall gods and men.
sections.bodyZh: 霍德尔站在人圈的外面，因为他是瞎子。洛基走过去问他：你为什么不朝巴德尔扔东西？霍德尔说：因为我看不见巴德尔在哪里，而且我也没有武器。洛基说：你也该像别人一样向巴德尔表示敬意。我来给你指方向，你把这根树枝向他扔去吧。霍德尔接过槲寄生，照着洛基的指引朝巴德尔扔去。树枝穿透了巴德尔的身体，他倒在地上死了。斯诺里说：这是神和人所遭遇的最大不幸。

sections.bodyEn: When Baldr fell, the Æsir were struck dumb and their hands failed them to lift him. Each looked at the other, all of one mind about who had done the deed, but no vengeance could be taken there, for it was a place of great sanctuary. When they tried to speak, weeping came first, and none could tell the others his grief. Odin bore the loss worst of all, for he best understood how great a loss and ruin Baldr's death was for the Æsir.
sections.bodyZh: 巴德尔倒下的时候，阿萨众神都说不出话来，双手也失去了力气，不能把他扶起。他们彼此相望，心里都知道是谁干了这件事，却不能在那里报仇，因为那是一处圣地。他们想说话的时候，涌出的只有泪水，没有一个神能把自己的悲痛告诉别人。在所有的神中，奥丁最承受不住这个打击，因为他最明白，巴德尔的死对阿萨众神意味着多大的损失与毁灭。

sections.bodyEn: When the gods came to themselves, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would win all her love and favour by riding the road to Hel to find Baldr and offer Hel a ransom to let him come home to Ásgarðr. Hermóðr the Bold, Odin's son, undertook the journey. Odin's horse Sleipnir was led out, and Hermóðr mounted and galloped away.
sections.bodyZh: 众神稍稍平静之后，弗丽嘉开口问道：阿萨神族中有谁愿意赢得我全部的爱与恩宠，骑马走上通往冥界的路，去找赫尔，问她要多少赎金才肯让巴德尔回到阿斯加德？奥丁的儿子、勇敢的赫尔莫德说他愿意去。于是众神牵来奥丁的八足骏马斯莱布尼尔，交给赫尔莫德。他跃上马背，向冥界疾驰而去。这是众神在巨大的悲痛中想到的唯一办法：如果冥界的女王肯收下赎金，巴德尔也许还能回来。赫尔莫德的马蹄声远去了，而留在阿斯加德的众神，还要先为巴德尔送行。

sections.bodyEn: The Æsir carried Baldr's body to the sea. His ship Hringhorni was the greatest of all ships, but they could not launch it, so they sent to Jötunheimr for the giantess Hyrrokkin, who came riding a wolf with vipers for reins. Four berserks could hold the wolf only by knocking it down. She pushed the ship off with one shove, so that fire flew from the rollers and the earth shook; Thor would have smashed her head had the gods not begged for her. When Baldr was laid on board, his wife Nanna's heart burst with grief, and she was laid on the pyre with him. Thor hallowed the pyre with Mjöllnir and kicked the dwarf Litr into the flames; Odin laid the ring Draupnir on the pyre, and Baldr's horse was burned with all its harness.
sections.bodyZh: 阿萨众神抬起巴德尔的尸体，送到海边。巴德尔的船叫作“灵钟号”，是所有船中最大的一艘，众神想把它推下海，在船上为巴德尔举行火葬，可是船纹丝不动。他们只好派人到巨人之国去请一个名叫希罗金的女巨人来帮忙。她骑着一头狼来了，用毒蛇作缰绳。她跳下狼背，奥丁叫四个狂战士看住那头狼，他们只能把它摔倒才制服它。希罗金走到船头，只一推就把船推下了海，船底的滚木冒出火花，大地都颤抖起来。索尔大怒，握住锤子要打碎她的头，众神都为她求情，他才住手。巴德尔的遗体被抬上船，他的妻子南娜看见了，悲痛得心都碎了，当场死去，也被放上柴堆一起焚烧。索尔站在火堆前用妙尔尼尔为它祝圣，一个名叫利特的矮人从他脚前跑过，索尔一脚把他踢进了火里。奥丁把金环德罗普尼尔放在柴堆上，巴德尔的马也带着全套马具被送上火堆。

sections.bodyEn: For nine nights Hermóðr rode through dark, deep valleys where he could see nothing, until he came to the river Gjöll and rode onto the Gjallarbrú, roofed with gleaming gold. The maiden who guarded the bridge, Móðguðr, asked his name and lineage: the day before, five companies of dead men had ridden over, yet the bridge thundered more under him alone, and he did not have the colour of the dead. He said he was riding to Hel to seek Baldr; she told him Baldr had crossed the bridge, and that the road to Hel lay downward and to the north.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德骑着马走了九天九夜，穿过幽深黑暗的山谷，什么也看不见，直到来到冥河耶尔河边，骑上了铺着闪亮黄金的耶尔桥。守桥的少女名叫莫德古德，她问他的名字和家族，说：昨天有五队死人从这座桥上过去，可是桥被你一个人震得比他们全体还响；而且你的脸色不像死人。你为什么骑马走在通往冥界的路上？赫尔莫德说：我要去冥界找巴德尔。你有没有在路上见过他？莫德古德说：巴德尔已经骑马过了耶尔桥。通往冥界的路，就在下面，往北边去。

sections.bodyEn: At Hel's gate Hermóðr dismounted, tightened the girth, remounted and spurred Sleipnir, who leapt clean over the gate. In the hall he saw his brother Baldr in the seat of honour, and stayed the night. In the morning he asked Hel to let Baldr ride home, telling of the gods' grief. Hel said she would test whether Baldr was as beloved as they said: if all things in the world, alive and dead, wept for him, he would return to the Æsir; but if any refused to weep, he would stay with Hel. Baldr gave Hermóðr the ring Draupnir to take to Odin as a keepsake, and Nanna sent Frigg a linen kerchief and Fulla a gold ring.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德一路骑到冥界的大门前，他跳下马，把马肚带勒紧，重新上马，用马刺一踢，骏马高高跃起，从大门上方越了过去，一点也没碰到。他骑到大殿前下了马，走进去，看见他的哥哥巴德尔坐在高座上。赫尔莫德在那里过了一夜。第二天早晨，他请求赫尔让巴德尔和他一起骑马回家，并告诉她阿萨众神为巴德尔哭得多么伤心。赫尔说：我要看看巴德尔是不是真的像人们说的那样受到爱戴。如果世上的一切东西，活的和死的，都为他哭泣，他就可以回到阿萨众神那里；可是只要有一样东西反对、不肯哭泣，他就得留在冥界。赫尔莫德起身告辞，巴德尔送他出殿，把金环德罗普尼尔交给他，让他带回去给奥丁作纪念；南娜也送给弗丽嘉一块亚麻头巾和其他礼物，还送给弗丽嘉的侍女富拉一枚金指环。

sections.bodyEn: Hermóðr rode back and told all he had seen and heard. The Æsir sent messengers throughout the world asking that Baldr be wept out of Hel. All things did so — men and beasts, the earth and stones, trees and every metal — as you will have seen these things weep when they come out of frost into warmth.
sections.bodyZh: 赫尔莫德骑马回到阿斯加德，把他的所见所闻原原本本地告诉了众神。于是阿萨众神派出使者走遍全世界，请求万物为巴德尔哭泣，好让他从冥界回来。万物都哭了：人和动物、大地和石头、树木和各种金属都哭了——斯诺里说，就像你看见这些东西从严寒中被拿到温暖的地方时，身上会凝出水珠来一样。使者们走遍了天上和人间，所到之处，没有一样东西不在流泪。众神满怀希望，以为巴德尔就要回来了。可是，就在使者们办完差事、踏上归途的时候，他们经过了一个山洞——

sections.bodyEn: As the messengers were returning, having done their errand well, they found a giantess sitting in a cave who called herself Þökk. They asked her to weep Baldr out of Hel. She answered: Þökk will weep dry tears for Baldr's burning; alive or dead, the old man's son was no use to me — let Hel keep what she has. Men believe she was Loki Laufeyjarson, who had done the Æsir the most harm. And so Baldr remained in Hel.
sections.bodyZh: 使者们完成了使命，正在回家的路上，看见一个山洞里坐着一个女巨人，她自称叫作索克。他们请她也为巴德尔哭泣，让他从冥界回来。她回答说：索克要流干的眼泪，为巴德尔的火葬哭泣。不论他是活着还是死了，我从这老头的儿子身上什么好处也没得到。让赫尔留着她已经得到的吧！人们都认为，这个女巨人就是劳菲之子洛基变的，他给阿萨众神带来了最多的灾祸。巴德尔就这样留在了冥界。
sections.headingEn: The giantess who would not weep
sections.uncertaintyNote: 斯诺里说“人们认为”索克就是洛基，这是传统中的认定，不是故事中直接揭穿的情节。

sections.bodyEn: The gods were so angry that Loki fled and built a house with four doors on a mountain so he could watch every way, and by day he often hid as a salmon in the Fránangr falls. Wondering how the gods might catch him, he knotted linen into a net — the first net — and when he saw the gods coming, threw it in the fire and leapt into the river. Kvasir, wisest of the gods, saw the shape of the net in the ashes, and they made one like it. Dragging the falls with Thor at one end, they drove Loki until he tried to leap over the net; Thor caught him in mid-air and held him by the tail, which is why the salmon tapers at the tail.
sections.bodyZh: 众神对洛基怒不可遏，洛基逃到一座山上，盖了一间有四扇门的房子，好向四面八方都能看见。白天他常常变成一条鲑鱼，躲进法拉南格瀑布里。他坐在屋里想：阿萨众神会用什么办法来抓瀑布里的鲑鱼呢？他拿起亚麻线，像人们后来做网那样结了一张网。这时他看见众神已经来到不远处，奥丁从高座上望见了他的藏身之处。洛基赶快把网扔进火里烧掉，跳进河中。最聪明的神克瓦西尔第一个走进屋里，看见火中网的灰烬，明白这是捕鱼的工具，众神就照着灰烬的样子结了一张网。他们来到瀑布边撒网，索尔握住一头，其余的神握住另一头。洛基几次从网下、从网上逃脱，最后一次他想跳过网逃向大海，索尔在空中一把抓住了他，他滑溜溜地往外挣，索尔紧紧捏住他的尾巴——据说正因为这样，鲑鱼的尾巴才变得那么细。

sections.bodyEn: The gods took Loki into a cave, set up three slabs on edge and bored a hole in each. They took his sons Váli and Nari (or Narfi); Váli was turned into a wolf and tore his brother apart, and with Nari's entrails they bound Loki over the stones — one under his shoulders, one under his loins, one under the backs of his knees — and the bonds became iron. Skaði hung a venomous snake above him so that its poison dripped onto his face. His wife Sigyn stands by holding a bowl under the venom, and when the bowl is full she goes to empty it; then the venom drips on his face and he shudders so violently that the whole earth shakes — what men call earthquakes. There he lies bound until Ragnarök.
sections.bodyZh: 众神把洛基带进一个山洞，竖起三块扁石，在每块石头上钻一个洞。他们抓来洛基的两个儿子瓦利和纳尔维，把瓦利变成一匹狼，狼把他的兄弟撕成了碎片。众神用纳尔维的肠子把洛基捆在三块石头上：一块抵着肩膀，一块抵着腰，一块抵着膝盖窝，那些肠子随后变成了铁。斯卡蒂拿来一条毒蛇，挂在洛基的头上方，让蛇的毒液滴在他脸上。洛基的妻子西格恩站在他身旁，手里捧着一只碗接住毒液；碗满了，她就走开去倒掉，这时毒液就滴在洛基的脸上，他痛得猛烈挣扎，整个大地都随之颤抖——这就是人们所说的地震。洛基就这样被捆着，一直躺到诸神的黄昏来临。

claims.statement: Baldr is killed by a shoot of mistletoe despite the oaths.
Frigg takes oaths from fire, water, metals, stones, plants and beasts not to harm Baldr, but not from the young mistletoe.
Frigg is Odin's wife and knows all fates, though she does not prophesy.
Gylfaginning presents Frigg as Baldr's mother in the account of his death.

events.summaryEn: Frigg is Odin's wife.
events.summaryZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。
events.titleEn: The goddess who knows all fates

events.summaryEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him.
events.summaryZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。

events.summaryEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him.
events.summaryZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。

sections.bodyEn: Frigg is Odin's wife. Snorri says she knows the fates of all, though she does not speak them aloud.
sections.bodyZh: 弗丽嘉是奥丁的妻子。斯诺里说，她知道一切人的命运，只是从不说出来。
sections.headingEn: The goddess who knows all fates

sections.bodyEn: Baldr has ominous dreams, so Frigg makes fire, water, iron and all metals, stones, earth, trees, sicknesses, beasts, birds and serpents swear not to harm him. Only a young mistletoe shoot she thinks too small to ask.
sections.bodyZh: 巴德尔做了不祥的梦。弗丽嘉便去找火、水、铁和各种金属、石头、土地、树木、疾病、野兽、鸟和蛇，让它们都发誓不伤害巴德尔。只有长在英灵殿西边的一株小槲寄生，她觉得太小，没有让它发誓。

sections.bodyEn: Believing Baldr unharmable, the gods amuse themselves by throwing things at him. But the mistletoe that never swore is made into a dart, and Baldr is struck down and dies.
sections.bodyZh: 众神以为巴德尔刀枪不入，便拿东西扔他取乐。然而那株没有发誓的槲寄生被做成了投枪，巴德尔被它刺中而死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 投掷者与幕后之人的情节将在后续批次逐段登记。

stories.canonicalTitle: The birth of Huitzilopochtli on Serpent Mountain
stories.editorialNote: 依据《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章（萨阿贡编纂，16世纪）；学者把这段故事与大神庙布局相联系属于解释层。
stories.summaryEn: While sweeping on Coatepec, Coatlicue picks up a ball of feathers, tucks it at her waist and conceives. Her daughter Coyolxauhqui, shamed, leads the four hundred brothers to kill their mother. As they reach the summit, Huitzilopochtli is born fully armed, beheads Coyolxauhqui and scatters the brothers.
stories.summaryZh: 科阿特利库埃在蛇山打扫时，一团羽毛飘落，她把它塞在腰间，因此怀孕。女儿科约尔沙乌基认为这是耻辱，带着四百个兄弟要杀死母亲。就在他们冲上山顶时，维齐洛波奇特利全副武装地出生，砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，把兄弟们赶散。
stories.titleZh: 蛇山上的诞生：维齐洛波奇特利

claims.statement: The birth and battle take place on Coatepec.
While sweeping on Coatepec, Coatlicue picks up a ball of feathers, places it at her waist and becomes pregnant.
Coyolxauhqui leads the attack on Coatepec.
Huitzilopochtli is born fully armed, with shield, darts and dart-thrower.
Huitzilopochtli beheads Coyolxauhqui and her body falls down the side of Coatepec.
He scatters the Centzon Huitznahua from the top of Coatepec.
Coyolxauhqui is a daughter of Coatlicue who urges her brothers, the Centzon Huitznahua, to kill their mother.
Huitzilopochtli is the child Coatlicue conceives at Coatepec.

entities.nameZh: 维齐洛波奇特利诞生于蛇山

events.summaryEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec.
events.summaryZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed.
events.summaryZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do.
events.summaryZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec.

sections.bodyEn: Coatlicue lives on Coatepec. One day as she sweeps, a ball of feathers drifts down. She picks it up and tucks it at her waist — and so she becomes pregnant.
sections.bodyZh: 科阿特利库埃住在蛇山上。一天她打扫时，一团羽毛从天上飘下来。她把羽毛捡起来，塞在腰间——就这样怀孕了。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: Her daughter Coyolxauhqui tells her brothers, the four hundred Centzon Huitznahua, that their mother has shamed them and must be killed. Armed, they set out for Coatepec.
sections.bodyZh: 她的女儿科约尔沙乌基对兄弟们——四百个南方人——说：母亲让我们蒙羞，我们必须杀了她。于是他们全副武装，朝蛇山进发。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: From the womb Huitzilopochtli comforts his mother: do not be afraid, I know what to do. The moment the attackers reach the summit he is born, carrying shield, darts and dart-thrower.
sections.bodyZh: 腹中的维齐洛波奇特利安慰母亲：不要怕，我知道该怎么做。敌人冲上山顶的那一刻，他出生了，手持盾牌、投枪和投枪器。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。

sections.bodyEn: Huitzilopochtli cuts off Coyolxauhqui's head, and her body tumbles down the side of Coatepec. He drives the four hundred brothers from the summit, scattering them in every direction.
sections.bodyZh: 维齐洛波奇特利砍下科约尔沙乌基的头，她的身体沿着蛇山滚落下去。四百个兄弟也被他从山顶追得四散奔逃。
sections.evidenceNote: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷第1章。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 学者认为这段叙事与大神庙的布局相呼应，属于解释，不写成事实。

stories.canonicalTitle: Quetzalcoatl and Titlacauan at Tollan
stories.editorialNote: 依据第三卷第2–5、14章的章节标题与概要；各章细节尚未逐段建模。
stories.summaryEn: Florentine Codex Book 3 tells of Quetzalcoatl, a great wizard at Tollan. Sorcerers come to him — among them Titlacauan, also called Tezcatlipoca — and their portents bring his glory to an end. As he departs, his followers freeze to death between two snow-capped volcanoes.
stories.summaryZh: 《佛罗伦萨手抄本》第三卷讲述图拉的大法师羽蛇神。巫师们来到他身边，其中一位叫蒂特拉卡瓦，也就是特斯卡特利波卡；他们带来的种种征兆让羽蛇神的荣光走向终结。羽蛇神离开时，随行的人在两座雪山之间冻死。
stories.titleZh: 图拉的羽蛇神与蒂特拉卡瓦

stories.canonicalTitle: Two gods on one pyramid — the Templo Mayor
stories.editorialNote: 现实遗址层：依据墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所（INAH）遗址博物馆的公开说明；不推测坐标。
stories.summaryEn: Atop the Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan stood two shrines: on the south, Huitzilopochtli, solar god of war and patron of the Mexica; on the north, Tlaloc, god of rain linked to agriculture. INAH says the first small temple was built at the city's founding in 1325 and was rebuilt and enlarged many times.
stories.summaryZh: 特诺奇蒂特兰的大神庙顶上并立着两座神殿：南边供奉太阳战神、墨西加人的守护神维齐洛波奇特利，北边供奉与农业相连的雨神特拉洛克。墨西哥国家人类学与历史研究所说，神庙始建于1325年，此后多次重建与扩建。
stories.titleZh: 一座金字塔上的两位神：大神庙

stories.canonicalTitle: Three Maya gods in stone, clay and glyph
stories.editorialNote: 三个版本分别来自联合国教科文组织遗产记录与大都会艺术博物馆的两份说明；不把玛雅与墨西加的羽蛇神合并。
stories.summaryEn: Three separate witnesses, one god each: Chichen-Itza's El Castillo is also called the Temple of Kukulkan; a Met plate shows the rain god Chahk waist-deep in water; and a Met exhibition presents the aged sky god Itzamnaaj and his bird avatar. They are read separately, not stitched into one myth.
stories.summaryZh: 三份独立见证，各讲一位玛雅神：奇琴伊察的卡斯蒂略金字塔又叫“库库尔坎神庙”；大都会博物馆的一只陶盘上，雨神恰克半身浸在水中；同一博物馆的展览介绍年老的天神伊察姆纳和他的鸟形化身。三份见证分开阅读，不拼成一个统一神话。
stories.titleZh: 石头、陶盘与文字中的三位玛雅神

sections.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆 2022 年展览说明。

sections.bodyEn: 'Itzamnaaj' is the name of a major deity in colonial Yucatán. The museum notes that how to read the Classic-period name glyph of this elderly god is still uncertain.
sections.bodyZh: “Itzamnaaj”是殖民时期尤卡坦一位重要神祇的名字。博物馆提醒，古典期这位老神的名字符号该怎样读，学界还没有定论。
sections.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆展览说明。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 名字读法未定，本站同时保留“伊察姆纳”与“Itzamnaaj”。

sections.bodyEn: This version rests on a modern exhibition text, not an ancient one. The exhibition says Itzamnaaj mattered in primordial myths but does not retell them, so the site does not fill in a plot.
sections.bodyZh: 这里依据的是一份现代展览介绍，而不是古代文本。展览说伊察姆纳在太初神话中很重要，但没有在说明里讲出那些神话；本站因此不替它补写情节。
sections.evidenceNote: 大都会艺术博物馆展览说明。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 待找到可定位的古代或殖民时期文本见证后再扩充。

stories.summaryEn: Gilgameš resolves to make his name in the mountains. His companion Enkidu warns that the mountains are Utu's concern, so the sun god must be told. stories.canonicalTitle: Fuxi makes the eight trigrams
stories.editorialNote: 依据《系辞下》第二章；“包牺即伏羲”采用传统注疏的读法。
stories.summaryEn: The Xi Ci II says that when Baoxi (Fuxi) ruled in antiquity, he looked up at heaven and down at the earth, studied the markings of birds and beasts and the land, drew on his own body and on distant things, and first made the eight trigrams; he also knotted cords into nets for hunting and fishing.
stories.summaryZh: 《周易·系辞下》说：古时包牺氏（伏羲）治理天下，他抬头观察天象，低头观察地理，看鸟兽身上的纹理和各地的物产，近取自身、远取万物，于是开始画出八卦；他又把绳子打结做成网，用来打猎捕鱼。
stories.titleZh: 伏羲始作八卦

claims.statement: The trigrams are made to communicate with the virtue of spirit-like intelligence and to classify the dispositions of the myriad things.
Xi Ci II is the textual witness for Baoxi's making of the trigrams.
The passage writes 包犧; reading Baoxi as Fuxi follows the traditional commentaries, which list 庖犧 and 伏戲 as variant forms.
Thereupon he first makes the eight trigrams (於是始作八卦).
Xi Ci II opens its account of the ancient sages with Baoxi (包犧氏) ruling all under heaven.
He knots cords to make nets for hunting and fishing.
He looks up at the images in heaven and down at the patterns on earth, observes the markings of birds and beasts and what suits the land, and takes from his own body and from things afar.

entities.canonicalName: Xi Ci commentary of the Zhouyi

events.summaryEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts.
events.summaryZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。
events.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

events.summaryEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for.
events.summaryZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。

events.summaryEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
events.summaryZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。

events.summaryEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish.
events.summaryZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。
events.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

sections.bodyEn: Xi Ci II lists the inventions of the ancient sages, and the first is Baoxi — usually written Fuxi in later texts. In remote antiquity, it says, he ruled all under heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 《系辞下》讲古代圣人的发明，第一位就是包牺氏——后世通常写作伏羲。书里说，远古的时候，是他在治理天下。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “包牺”即“伏羲”是传统注疏的读法。

sections.bodyEn: He looked up at the images in the sky and down at the patterns of the earth; he studied the markings of birds and beasts and what each land was suited for. Near at hand he drew on his own body, and far off on all things.
sections.bodyZh: 他抬头观察天上的日月星辰，低头观察大地的形势；又细看鸟兽身上的花纹，看各地适合生长什么。近处，他从自己的身体取法；远处，他从万物取法。

sections.bodyEn: Thereupon he first made the eight trigrams — eight figures of three lines each — to communicate with spirit-like virtue and to sort the dispositions of the myriad things.
sections.bodyZh: 于是他开始画出八卦——八个由三条线组成的符号，用来通达神明的德性，把万物的情状分门别类。
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“于是始作八卦”。

sections.bodyEn: He also knotted cords into nets, which people used to hunt and fish. The Xi Ci then moves on to later sages such as Shennong; this retelling covers only Baoxi's part.
sections.bodyZh: 他还把绳子打结，做成罗网，人们用它打猎、捕鱼。《系辞》接下来再讲神农等后来的圣人，这里只讲伏羲这一段。
sections.evidenceNote: 《系辞下》第二章“作结绳而为罔罟”。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 后续圣人的发明不在本故事范围内。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Yellow Emperor and Chiyou at Zhuolu
stories.editorialNote: 依据《史记·五帝本纪》；司马迁以史笔叙述，本站只登记文本所述，不作历史真实性断言。
stories.summaryEn: The Shiji's Annals of the Five Emperors say that as Shennong's house declined and the lords fought one another, Xuanyuan trained troops. Chiyou, the most violent, rebelled against the ruler's command; Xuanyuan levied the lords' armies, captured and killed him in the wilds of Zhuolu, and was honoured as Son of Heaven — the Yellow Emperor.
stories.summaryZh: 《史记·五帝本纪》说：神农氏衰落，诸侯互相攻伐，轩辕操练军队征讨不服者。蚩尤最为暴虐，作乱不听帝命。轩辕征召诸侯之兵，在涿鹿的原野擒杀蚩尤，诸侯于是尊他为天子，这就是黄帝。
stories.titleZh: 黄帝战蚩尤：涿鹿之战

claims.statement: As the house of Shennong declines and the lords attack one another, Xuanyuan trains troops to punish those who do not bring tribute.
The Annals of the Five Emperors are the textual witness used for the Zhuolu episode.
Chiyou is the most violent of the lords; he rebels and does not obey the ruler's command.
The Shiji introduces the Yellow Emperor as the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan.
He finally captures and kills Chiyou (遂禽殺蚩尤).
The lords all honour Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong; this is the Yellow Emperor.
Chiyou is the opponent at Zhuolu.
The Yellow Emperor levies the lords' troops and fights Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu.

sections.bodyEn: The Yellow Emperor was the son of Shaodian, surnamed Gongsun and named Xuanyuan. In his time the rule of Shennong had declined; the lords attacked one another and oppressed the people, and Shennong could not punish them. So Xuanyuan trained troops to subdue the lords who would not pay tribute.
sections.bodyZh: 黄帝是少典的儿子，姓公孙，名轩辕。他那个时代，神农氏的统治衰落了，诸侯互相攻打、欺压百姓，神农氏却无力征讨。轩辕于是操练军队，去讨伐不肯朝贡的诸侯。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 此前轩辕与炎帝在阪泉的三次交战本故事未展开。

sections.bodyEn: Among the lords Chiyou was the most violent, and no one could subdue him. Chiyou rose in rebellion and would not obey the ruler's command.
sections.bodyZh: 诸侯之中，蚩尤最为凶暴，没有人能制服他。蚩尤起来作乱，不听从帝王的命令。
sections.evidenceNote: 《五帝本纪》“蚩尤作乱，不用帝命”。

sections.bodyEn: Xuanyuan called up the armies of the lords and fought Chiyou in the wilds of Zhuolu, and at last captured and killed him.
sections.bodyZh: 轩辕征召各路诸侯的军队，在涿鹿的原野上与蚩尤交战，终于把蚩尤擒住并杀死。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 涿鹿不在本站映射为现代坐标。

sections.bodyEn: The lords all honoured Xuanyuan as Son of Heaven in place of Shennong: this was the Yellow Emperor.
sections.bodyZh: 诸侯们都尊奉轩辕为天子，取代了神农氏，这就是黄帝。

stories.canonicalTitle: Pangu between heaven and earth
stories.editorialNote: 依据《艺文类聚》卷一所引《三五历纪》，并以《太平御览》卷一的引文对照；盘古身体化生万物另见他书，不在此合并。
stories.summaryEn: Xu Zheng's Sanwu liji is lost, surviving only in later encyclopedias. Yiwen leiju juan 1 quotes it: before heaven and earth parted, all was chaos like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside; after 18,000 years they opened, clear becoming heaven and murky becoming earth; each day heaven rose a zhang, earth thickened a zhang and Pangu grew a zhang, until after another 18,000 years heaven was highest, earth deepest and Pangu tallest.
stories.summaryZh: 三国吴人徐整的《三五历纪》已经失传，只在后世类书中留有引文。《艺文类聚》卷一引它说：天地未分时混沌如鸡蛋，盘古生在其中；一万八千年后天地开辟，清者为天、浊者为地；天每天高一丈，地每天厚一丈，盘古每天长一丈，又过一万八千年，天极高、地极深、盘古极长。
stories.titleZh: 盘古开天地：《三五历纪》佚文

claims.statement: This story uses only the Sanwu liji quotation; the motif of Pangu's dying body becoming sun, moon, rivers and mountains comes from a different text and is not merged here.
The Sanwu liji is lost; its Pangu passage is known through quotations in later encyclopedias such as Yiwen leiju juan 1 and Taiping yulan juan 1.
Before heaven and earth separate, all is chaos like a hen's egg, and Pangu is born within it.

Each day heaven rises one zhang, earth thickens one zhang and Pangu grows one zhang; after another 18,000 years heaven is extremely high, earth extremely deep and Pangu extremely tall. Only afterwards come the Three Sovereigns.
After 18,000 years heaven and earth open: the clear yang becomes heaven, the murky yin becomes earth, and Pangu is between them, changing nine times a day.

entities.canonicalName: Pangu between heaven and earth (Sanwu liji)

events.summaryEn: Long ago heaven and earth were not yet apart; everything was one chaos shaped like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside it.
events.summaryZh: 很久以前，天和地还没有分开，到处是一团混沌，样子像一个鸡蛋。
events.uncertaintyNote: 原书已佚，只能依靠类书引文。

events.summaryEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth.
events.summaryZh: 过了一万八千年，天地开辟：轻而清的阳气上升成为天，重而浊的阴气下沉成为地。

events.summaryEn: From then on heaven rose a zhang each day, earth grew a zhang thicker, and Pangu grew a zhang taller.
events.summaryZh: 从此天每天升高一丈，地每天加厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。
events.uncertaintyNote: “盘古垂死化身为日月山川”出自另一部书，本故事不合并。

sections.bodyEn: Long ago heaven and earth were not yet apart; everything was one chaos shaped like a hen's egg, and Pangu was born inside it.
sections.bodyZh: 很久以前，天和地还没有分开，到处是一团混沌，样子像一个鸡蛋。盘古就生在这团混沌之中。
sections.evidenceNote: 《艺文类聚》卷一引《三五历纪》；《太平御览》卷一引文字句略异。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 原书已佚，只能依靠类书引文。

sections.bodyEn: After 18,000 years heaven and earth opened: the light, clear yang rose to become heaven, the heavy, murky yin sank to become earth. Pangu stood between them, changing nine times a day, more divine than heaven and wiser than earth.
sections.bodyZh: 过了一万八千年，天地开辟：轻而清的阳气上升成为天，重而浊的阴气下沉成为地。盘古就在天地之间，一天之中变化九次，比天更神，比地更圣。
sections.evidenceNote: 同一引文“阳清为天，阴浊为地”。

sections.bodyEn: From then on heaven rose a zhang each day, earth grew a zhang thicker, and Pangu grew a zhang taller. After another 18,000 years heaven was as high as it could be, earth as deep, and Pangu as tall. Only after that came the Three Sovereigns.
sections.bodyZh: 从此天每天升高一丈，地每天加厚一丈，盘古也每天长高一丈。这样又过了一万八千年，天高到了极点，地深到了极点，盘古也长到了极点。在这之后，才有了三皇。
sections.evidenceNote: 同一引文“天日高一丈……盘古日长一丈”。
sections.uncertaintyNote: “盘古垂死化身为日月山川”出自另一部书，本故事不合并。

stories.canonicalTitle: Nezha against Sun Wukong (Journey to the West, ch. 4)
stories.editorialNote: 明代小说《西游记》属于后世文学接受层，不当作古代神话见证；哪吒闹海等故事出自其他作品，未在此合并。
stories.summaryEn: Finding his stable post too lowly, Sun Wukong returns home and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven. Heavenly King Li and his third son Nezha are sent to seize him. Nezha takes three heads and six arms; Wukong does the same, then turns a hair into a double and strikes Nezha from behind, and Nezha retreats in pain.
stories.summaryZh: 孙悟空嫌弼马温官小，回花果山自称齐天大圣。托塔李天王与哪吒三太子奉命捉拿。哪吒变出三头六臂，悟空也变三头六臂；悟空拔毫毛变出分身，真身绕到背后打中哪吒，哪吒负痛败走。
stories.titleZh: 哪吒大战孙悟空：《西游记》第四回

claims.statement: Nezha shouts and changes into a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in each hand.
In chapter 4 Nezha appears as the third prince who accompanies Heavenly King Li, the pagoda-bearer, against Sun Wukong.
Wukong plucks a hair to make a double that keeps fighting, circles behind Nezha with his true body and strikes him; Nezha retreats in pain.
Nezha is sent with Heavenly King Li to capture the self-styled Great Sage.
Sun Wukong, having called himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven, fights Nezha.
Wukong also takes three heads and six arms and turns his staff into three to parry.

entities.canonicalName: Nezha fights Sun Wukong (Journey to the West ch. 4)
entities.nameZh: 哪吒大战孙悟空（《西游记》第四回）

events.summaryEn: Discovering that his title merely made him a keeper of horses, Sun Wukong storms back to his mountain and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven.
events.summaryZh: 孙悟空发现“弼马温”只是个看马的小官，一气之下回到花果山，自称“齐天大圣”。

events.summaryEn: Nezha gives a shout and becomes a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in every hand.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒大喝一声，变成三头六臂，六只手各拿一件兵器打来。

events.summaryEn: Neither can win.
events.summaryZh: 两人斗得难分难解。
events.uncertaintyNote: 这是小说情节，属于后世文学层。

sections.bodyEn: Discovering that his title merely made him a keeper of horses, Sun Wukong storms back to his mountain and calls himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven. The Jade Emperor sends Heavenly King Li, bearer of the pagoda, and his third son Nezha with the heavenly troops to seize him.
sections.bodyZh: 孙悟空发现“弼马温”只是个看马的小官，一气之下回到花果山，自称“齐天大圣”。玉帝派托塔李天王和他的三太子哪吒，带领天兵前去捉拿。

sections.bodyEn: Nezha gives a shout and becomes a figure with three heads and six arms, a weapon in every hand. Wukong does the same: he shakes his staff into three and parries with six hands.
sections.bodyZh: 哪吒大喝一声，变成三头六臂，六只手各拿一件兵器打来。悟空见了，也变成三头六臂，把金箍棒一晃变成三条，六只手拿着架住。

sections.bodyEn: Neither can win. Wukong plucks a hair and turns it into a double of himself to keep fighting, while his true body circles behind Nezha and strikes. Nezha flees in pain and reports to his father that the monkey's powers are great.
sections.bodyZh: 两人斗得难分难解。悟空拔下一根毫毛，变成自己的模样继续迎敌，真身却绕到哪吒背后打了一棒。哪吒负痛败走，回去禀报父王：这猴子神通广大。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是小说情节，属于后世文学层。

stories.canonicalTitle: The Second Battle of Mag Tuired
stories.editorialNote: 依据 Elizabeth A. Gray 1982 年校译本（CELT T300010）的段落编号；译文受版权保护，只发布定位与独立概述。
stories.summaryEn: The medieval Irish saga Cath Maige Tuired: the Dagda's cauldron leaves no one unsatisfied; Lug, master of all arts, comes to Tara; at Samain the Dagda meets the Morrígan by the river; Bríg keens for her slain son, the first keening in Ireland; Lug's sling stone drives Balor's deadly eye through his head; and the Morrígan proclaims the victory across Ireland.
stories.summaryZh: 中世纪爱尔兰传说《第二次马格图雷德之战》：达格达拥有“没有人吃不饱”的大锅；“百艺之主”鲁格来到塔拉；萨温节时达格达在河边遇见莫莉甘；布里格为战死的儿子哀哭，是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌；鲁格用投石击毁巴洛尔的毒眼；战后莫莉甘向全爱尔兰宣告胜利。
stories.titleZh: 第二次马格图雷德之战：达格达、莫莉甘、布里格与鲁格

claims.statement: Balor has a destructive eye that is opened only on the battlefield; four men lift its lid with a polished handle.
No company ever went away from the Dagda's cauldron unsatisfied.
Cath Maige Tuired is the textual witness for the second battle of Mag Tuired.
When Rúadán is killed, Bríg comes and keens for her son, first shrieking and then weeping: the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
Among the four treasures of the Túatha Dé Danann, the Dagda's cauldron was brought from Murias.
At Samain the Dagda meets the Morrígan washing at the Unshin, one foot on each bank; they unite, and she tells him where the Fomoire will land.
Lug casts a sling stone that drives Balor's eye through the back of his head, so that it is Balor's own host that looks upon it.
Arriving at Tara, Lug is admitted as the one who possesses every art at once: the Samildánach.
After the battle the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, chief waters and river-mouths, and then prophesies.
Rúadán is the son of Bres and of Bríg, the Dagda's daughter.
The Dagda takes part in the preparations and the battle.
Lug fights in the battle and faces Balor.
The Morrígan aids the Túatha Dé Danann and proclaims the victory.
The Morrígan promises to destroy the Fomorian king Indech, taking the blood of his heart and the kidneys of his valour.

entities.nameZh: 第二次马格图雷德之战

entities.canonicalName: Cath Maige Tuired (The Second Battle of Mag Tuired)

events.summaryEn: The Túatha Dé Danann brought four treasures.
events.summaryZh: 达努神族带来了四件宝物，其中一件是从穆里亚斯城带来的达格达的大锅：凡是围着它吃饭的人，从没有一个是不饱足地离开的。

events.summaryEn: Lug comes to the door of Tara, and the doorkeeper asks what art he brings.
events.summaryZh: 鲁格来到塔拉的大门前，守门人问他会什么手艺。
events.titleEn: The master of all arts at Tara

events.summaryEn: Around Samain the Dagda meets a woman washing at the river Unshin, one foot on the southern bank and one on the northern.
events.summaryZh: 萨温节前后，达格达在乌恩辛河边遇见一个女人正在洗东西，一只脚踩在南岸，一只脚踩在北岸。

events.summaryEn: Rúadán, son of Bres and of Bríg the Dagda's daughter, is sent to kill the smith Goibniu and is killed instead.
events.summaryZh: 布里格是达格达的女儿，她和布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹被派去刺杀铁匠戈伊布纽，却被戈伊布纽杀死。
events.uncertaintyNote: 文本写作 Bríg；与数据库中“布里吉德”实体的对应依学界通行用法。

events.summaryEn: The Fomorian champion Balor has a deadly eye, opened only on the battlefield, its lid lifted by four men with a handle.
events.summaryZh: 弗魔族勇士巴洛尔有一只毒眼，只在战场上睁开，要四个人用把手才能抬起眼皮。

events.summaryEn: When the battle is won, the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, its chief waters and river-mouths — and then speaks prophecy.
events.summaryZh: 战斗结束后，恩玛斯的女儿莫莉甘把这场大胜宣告给爱尔兰的王者高地、神丘里的众灵、各条大河与河口，然后又说出关于未来的预言。
events.uncertaintyNote: 预言诗的内容未逐句建模。

versions.narrativeScope: 四宝、鲁格入塔拉、萨温之约、布里格哀哭、巴洛尔之死与莫莉甘的宣告
versions.rightsNote: Gray 译文受版权保护；只发布段落定位与独立概述。

sections.bodyEn: The Túatha Dé Danann brought four treasures. One was the Dagda's cauldron from the city of Murias: no company that ate from it ever went away unsatisfied.
sections.bodyZh: 达努神族带来了四件宝物，其中一件是从穆里亚斯城带来的达格达的大锅：凡是围着它吃饭的人，从没有一个是不饱足地离开的。

sections.bodyEn: Lug comes to the door of Tara, and the doorkeeper asks what art he brings. He names one after another, and each already has a master within — until he asks whether anyone there has all of them at once. So he is admitted as the Samildánach, master of all arts.
sections.bodyZh: 鲁格来到塔拉的大门前，守门人问他会什么手艺。他报出一门又一门，而宫里每门手艺都已有人；最后他问：有没有一个人能同时精通所有这些？于是他以“百艺之主”的身份被请了进去。
sections.headingEn: The master of all arts at Tara

sections.bodyEn: Around Samain the Dagda meets a woman washing at the river Unshin, one foot on the southern bank and one on the northern. She is the Morrígan. After they unite she tells him where the Fomoire will land and promises to take the heart's blood of their king Indech.
sections.bodyZh: 萨温节前后，达格达在乌恩辛河边遇见一个女人正在洗东西，一只脚踩在南岸，一只脚踩在北岸。她就是莫莉甘。两人结合之后，她告诉达格达弗魔族将在哪里登陆，并许诺要取弗魔王因德赫的心血。

sections.bodyEn: Rúadán, son of Bres and of Bríg the Dagda's daughter, is sent to kill the smith Goibniu and is killed instead. Bríg comes and keens for her son, shrieking first and weeping at the end — the first time keening and weeping were heard in Ireland.
sections.bodyZh: 布里格是达格达的女儿，她和布雷斯的儿子鲁阿丹被派去刺杀铁匠戈伊布纽，却被戈伊布纽杀死。布里格赶来为儿子哀哭，先是尖声恸哭，最后低声啜泣——这是爱尔兰第一次听到哀歌与哭泣。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 文本写作 Bríg；与数据库中“布里吉德”实体的对应依学界通行用法。

sections.bodyEn: The Fomorian champion Balor has a deadly eye, opened only on the battlefield, its lid lifted by four men with a handle. Lug casts a sling stone that drives the eye out through the back of Balor's head, so that it is his own host that looks upon it.
sections.bodyZh: 弗魔族勇士巴洛尔有一只毒眼，只在战场上睁开，要四个人用把手才能抬起眼皮。鲁格用投石一击，石头把那只眼睛从巴洛尔脑后打了出去，结果看见它的反而是他自己的军队。

sections.bodyEn: When the battle is won, the Morrígan, daughter of Ernmas, proclaims the great victory to the royal heights of Ireland, its síd-hosts, its chief waters and river-mouths — and then speaks prophecy.
sections.bodyZh: 战斗结束后，恩玛斯的女儿莫莉甘把这场大胜宣告给爱尔兰的王者高地、神丘里的众灵、各条大河与河口，然后又说出关于未来的预言。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 预言诗的内容未逐句建模。

stories.canonicalTitle: The idols on the Kyiv hill — Perun and Mokosh
stories.editorialNote: 依据《往年纪事》980 与 988 年条；编年史由皈依后的基督教修士编写，对旧信仰的描述带有立场；莫科什在此只有名字。
stories.summaryEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980: Volodimer sets up idols on the hill outside his Kyiv palace — a wooden Perun with a silver head and golden moustache, then Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Simargl and Mokosh — and people make offerings to them. After his baptism in 988 he has them cast down; Perun is tied to a horse's tail, dragged down the hill and thrown into the Dnieper.
stories.summaryZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条：弗拉基米尔在基辅宫殿外的山岗上立起神像——银头金须的木雕佩伦，还有霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔和莫科什，人们向它们献祭。988 年他受洗后下令推倒神像，佩伦被绑在马尾上拖下山，丢进第聂伯河。
stories.titleZh: 基辅山岗上的神像：佩伦与莫科什

claims.statement: The chronicle gives Mokosh's name but no story, function or image; it was written by Christian clergy after the conversion.
Mokosh is the last name in the 980 list of idols: Perun, Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog, Simargl and Mokosh.
In 988 Volodimer orders the idols overthrown; Perun's image is tied to a horse's tail, beaten with sticks, dragged down the hill and thrown into the Dnieper.
The 980 annal records Volodimer setting up idols on the hill outside the palace hall in Kyiv.
The 980 annal describes a wooden Perun idol with a silver head and golden moustache on the Kyiv hill.
Mokosh is one of the idols Volodimer sets up on the Kyiv hill, to which people make offerings.
Perun heads the 980 list of idols on the Kyiv hill.

entities.canonicalName: Volodimer's idols on the Kyiv hill (980)
The Kyiv idols are cast down (988)

events.summaryEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980 records that when Volodimer began to reign alone in Kyiv, he set up a row of idols on the hill outside the palace courtyard.
events.summaryZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条记载：弗拉基米尔开始在基辅独自为王，就在宫殿庭院外的山岗上立起一排神像。

events.summaryEn: First stood Perun, carved of wood, with a silver head and a golden moustache.
events.summaryZh: 最前面的是佩伦：木头雕成，头是银的，胡须是金的。

events.summaryEn: Then came Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog and Simargl, and last on the list, Mokosh.
events.summaryZh: 接下来是霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔，名单的最后一位是莫科什。
events.titleEn: Mokosh at the end of the list
events.uncertaintyNote: 关于莫科什职能的说法来自其他材料与现代研究，本故事不补写。

events.summaryEn: Eight years later Volodimer was baptized and ordered the idols overthrown — some cut to pieces, others burned.
events.summaryZh: 八年后，弗拉基米尔受洗，下令推倒这些神像：有的砍碎，有的烧掉。
events.uncertaintyNote: 这是皈依一方的记载，不是对斯拉夫宗教的中立描述。

versions.narrativeScope: 山岗神像、神名名单与 988 年毁像
versions.rightsNote: 只发布年条定位与独立概述。

sections.bodyEn: The Primary Chronicle's annal for 980 records that when Volodimer began to reign alone in Kyiv, he set up a row of idols on the hill outside the palace courtyard.
sections.bodyZh: 《往年纪事》980 年条记载：弗拉基米尔开始在基辅独自为王，就在宫殿庭院外的山岗上立起一排神像。

sections.bodyEn: First stood Perun, carved of wood, with a silver head and a golden moustache.
sections.bodyZh: 最前面的是佩伦：木头雕成，头是银的，胡须是金的。

sections.bodyEn: Then came Khors, Dazhbog, Stribog and Simargl, and last on the list, Mokosh. People brought offerings to the idols. The chronicle records only Mokosh's name, not what she governed.
sections.bodyZh: 接下来是霍尔斯、达日博格、斯特里博格、西马尔格尔，名单的最后一位是莫科什。人们向这些神像献上祭品。编年史只记下了莫科什的名字，没有说她掌管什么。
sections.evidenceNote: 《往年纪事》980 年条神名名单。
sections.headingEn: Mokosh at the end of the list
sections.uncertaintyNote: 关于莫科什职能的说法来自其他材料与现代研究，本故事不补写。

sections.bodyEn: Eight years later Volodimer was baptized and ordered the idols overthrown — some cut to pieces, others burned. Perun was tied to a horse's tail and dragged down the hill, beaten with sticks, and thrown into the Dnieper.
sections.bodyZh: 八年后，弗拉基米尔受洗，下令推倒这些神像：有的砍碎，有的烧掉。佩伦被绑在马尾上拖下山，有人用棍子抽打，最后被扔进第聂伯河。
sections.uncertaintyNote: 这是皈依一方的记载，不是对斯拉夫宗教的中立描述。

stories.canonicalTitle: Mithra of the wide pastures — the Mihr Yasht
stories.editorialNote: 依据达梅斯特泰尔译本（avesta.org）第10颂第1、2、7、13节；现代学者对诗句的理解另有讨论。
stories.summaryEn: The Mihr Yasht, tenth hymn of the Avesta: Ahura Mazda says he made Mithra as worthy of sacrifice and prayer as himself; whoever lies to Mithra and breaks the contract brings death to the whole land; Mithra has a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes and is the first god to rise over Mount Hara, before the swift-horsed sun.
stories.summaryZh: 阿维斯塔第十颂《密赫尔颂》：阿胡拉·马兹达说，他创造密特拉时，使他与自己同样值得祭祀和祈祷；对密特拉说谎、背弃契约的人会给整个国家带来死亡；密特拉有千只耳朵、万只眼睛，在不朽的快马太阳之前最先越过哈拉山。
stories.titleZh: 广阔牧场之主密特拉：《密赫尔颂》

claims.statement: The Mihr Yasht is Yasht 10 of the Avesta.
The hymn repeatedly calls Mithra 'lord of wide pastures'.
The one who lies to Mithra — who breaks the contract — brings death to the whole land; the contract must be kept with the faithful and the unfaithful alike.
Ahura Mazda tells Zarathustra that when he created Mithra, lord of wide pastures, he made him as worthy of sacrifice and prayer as himself.
Mithra is truth-speaking, a chief in assemblies, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes.
He is the first of the heavenly gods to reach over Mount Hara, before the undying swift-horsed sun.

events.summaryEn: The hymn opens with Ahura Mazda telling Zarathustra: when I created Mithra, lord of wide pastures, I made him as worthy of sacrifice and as worthy of prayer as myself.
events.summaryZh: 颂歌一开头，阿胡拉·马兹达对查拉图斯特拉说：我创造广阔牧场之主密特拉时，使他与我自己一样，值得献祭、值得祈祷。

events.summaryEn: The wretch who lies to Mithra, breaking the contract, brings death upon the whole land.
events.summaryZh: 对密特拉说谎、背弃契约的恶人，会给整个国家带来死亡。
events.uncertaintyNote: “契约”是译者对 miθra 一词的理解，学界另有讨论。

events.summaryEn: The hymn praises Mithra as truth-speaking, a chief in assemblies, with a thousand ears and ten thousand eyes — nothing escapes him.
events.summaryZh: 颂歌赞美密特拉说真话，是集会中的首领；他有一千只耳朵，一万只眼睛，什么都瞒不过他。
events.titleEn: A thousand ears, ten thousand eyes

events.summaryEn: Each morning he is the first of the heavenly gods to reach over Mount Hara, ahead of the undying, swift-horsed sun.
events.summaryZh: 每天清晨，他是天上诸神中第一个越过哈拉山的，比不朽的、驾着快马的太阳还要早。

stories.canonicalTitle: Sixteen good lands and their plagues — Videvdad 1
stories.editorialNote: 依据达梅斯特泰尔译本（avesta.org）第一章；译者认为这是伊朗的宗教地理，而不是迁徙记录。
stories.summaryEn: Videvdad 1: Ahura Mazda makes sixteen good lands, the first being Airyana Vaejah by the good river Daitya; for each, Angra Mainyu, who is all death, counter-creates a plague — the serpent in the river and winter for the first, the locust for the second.
stories.summaryZh: 《万迪达德》第一章：阿胡拉·马兹达创造了十六片良地，第一片是善河岱提亚旁的雅利安瓦伊贾；每创造一片，“全然是死亡”的安格拉·曼纽就造出一种灾祸与之对抗——第一片是河中之蛇和寒冬，第二片是蝗虫。
stories.titleZh: 十六片良地与它们的灾祸：《万迪达德》第一章

claims.statement: Darmesteter argues the chapter is a religious geography of Iran mixing mythic lands and real countries, not a record of migrations; only some lands can be identified.
Ahura Mazda says the first of the good lands he created was Airyana Vaejah, by the good river Daitya.
Then Angra Mainyu, who is all death, counter-creates the serpent in the river and winter, a work of the daevas.
The list continues land by land — the second, the plains of the Sughdhas, is answered by the locust — until sixteen lands and sixteen plagues are named.
Ahura Mazda makes the sixteen good lands.
Angra Mainyu sets a counter-creation against each land.
Throughout Videvdad 1 every good land made by Ahura Mazda is answered by a plague from Angra Mainyu.

stories.canonicalTitle: Pele's journey to Halemaʻumaʻu
stories.editorialNote: 须署名的公开概述：依据美国国家公园管理局两页公开介绍；各家族与地方的 moʻolelo 版本差异很大，本站不收集。
stories.summaryEn: The National Park Service summarizes Hawaiian oral history: the volcano deity Pele was born in distant Kahiki and voyaged to the Hawaiian Islands seeking a home for her fire and family, moving southeast until she settled in Halemaʻumaʻu crater at the summit of Kīlauea, where she is said still to live. In Hawaiian tradition one asks her permission to travel through her land.
stories.summaryZh: 美国国家公园管理局概述夏威夷口述传统：火山女神佩蕾生在遥远的卡希基，为寻找适合她的火与家人的居所，远航来到夏威夷群岛，一路向东南迁移，最后在基拉韦厄山顶的哈雷茂茂火山口安家，据说至今仍住在那里。按照夏威夷传统，经过她的土地要先请求许可。
stories.titleZh: 佩蕾的旅程：从卡希基到哈雷茂茂

claims.statement: NPS describes Pele as the Hawaiian volcano deity, an elemental force and the creator of the volcanic landscapes.
NPS notes that different versions of the moʻolelo may vary, in some cases significantly; this story follows only the park's public summary.
Pele's permanent home is Halemaʻumaʻu crater at the summit of Kīlauea, where she is said still to reside.
Oral history says Pele was born in the distant land of Kahiki and voyaged to the Hawaiian Islands in search of a suitable home.
In Hawaiian tradition it is customary to ask Pele's permission to travel through her land, and NPS asks visitors to behave respectfully in this sacred landscape.
She migrates southeast through the islands before reaching Kīlauea.

stories.canonicalTitle: The Monkey King: from the stone egg to Havoc in Heaven
stories.editorialNote: 明代小说属于后世文学接受层；本站按回目顺序独立讲述，不当作古代神话见证。
stories.summaryEn: The full opening arc of Journey to the West: a stone on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit gives birth to a monkey who becomes king of the Water Curtain Cave, crosses the seas to learn immortality, the seventy-two transformations and the somersault cloud, takes the iron staff from the Dragon King, strikes his name from the register of death, scorns heaven's offices, eats the peaches and elixir, defeats heaven's armies, survives the furnace with fiery golden eyes, and is finally pinned under the Mountain of Five Elements by Rulai.
stories.summaryZh: 《西游记》前七回的完整讲述：花果山仙石孕出石猴，他在水帘洞称王，又为躲避死亡漂洋求道，从须菩提祖师那里学会七十二变和筋斗云；回山后到龙宫取走如意金箍棒，在地府勾掉生死簿；天庭先封他弼马温、后封齐天大圣，他却偷吃蟠桃和金丹，打退十万天兵；最后被二郎神擒住，八卦炉炼出火眼金睛，终被如来压在五行山下。
stories.titleZh: 美猴王：从石猴出世到大闹天宫

claims.statement: A stone on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit splits into a stone egg that becomes a monkey whose eyes flash light to heaven.
The stone monkey leaps through the waterfall, finds the Water Curtain Cave and is acclaimed Handsome Monkey King.
Grieving that the King of the Dead will one day claim him, the Monkey King sails alone across the sea to seek immortality.
Patriarch Subodhi receives the monkey at the Cave of the Slanting Moon and Three Stars and names him Sun Wukong.
Understanding the patriarch's three blows as a riddle, Wukong is secretly taught long life, the seventy-two transformations and the somersault cloud.
After Wukong shows off by becoming a pine tree, the patriarch expels him and forbids him ever to name his teacher.
Ao Guang, Dragon King of the Eastern Sea, lets Sun Wukong take the 13,500-pound iron that becomes the Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod.
Dragged to the underworld in a dream, Wukong strikes his own name and those of all monkeys from the Register of Life and Death.
On Venus's advice the Jade Emperor summons Wukong to heaven and appoints him Keeper of the Heavenly Horses, a post without rank.
After Heavenly King Li and Nezha fail to capture him, the Jade Emperor grants Wukong the empty title Great Sage Equal to Heaven and builds him a mansion.
Put in charge of the Garden of Immortal Peaches, Wukong secretly eats the ripest peaches and learns he is not invited to the Peach Banquet.
Wukong drinks the banquet wine, eats Laozi's elixir pills and holds off a hundred thousand heavenly soldiers at his mountain.
Erlang matches every transformation of the Great Sage until Laozi's Diamond Snare and Erlang's hound bring him down.
Laozi refines the captured Great Sage in his Eight Trigrams furnace for forty-nine days; he emerges with fiery golden eyes and kicks the furnace over.
Rulai wagers that the Great Sage cannot somersault out of his right palm; the monkey leaps and reaches five pink pillars he takes for the edge of heaven.
Rulai reveals the Great Sage's graffiti on his own finger and turns his hand into the Mountain of Five Elements, pinning the monkey beneath it.

events.summaryEn: Beyond the sea from the land of Aolai on the Eastern Continent stands the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, and on its summit an immortal stone that had absorbed the essences of heaven and earth since the world began.
events.summaryZh: 东胜神洲傲来国的海外，有一座花果山，山顶上立着一块仙石。
events.titleEn: A stone gives birth to a monkey

events.summaryEn: The raft carried him to the Southern Continent, where for eight or nine years he learned human speech and dress but met only people chasing fame and profit.
events.summaryZh: 木筏被风吹到南赡部洲。
events.titleEn: The Cave of the Slanting Moon and Three Stars
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Wukong swept, fetched water and cut wood for six or seven years.
events.summaryZh: 悟空在洞中扫地、挑水、砍柴，一住就是六七年。
events.titleEn: A secret lesson at the third watch
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: One evening his fellow students begged to see his new powers, and Wukong turned himself into a pine tree to their loud applause.
events.summaryZh: 一天傍晚，众师兄围着悟空，要看他学来的变化。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Needing a weapon, Wukong dived to the Crystal Palace of Ao Guang, Dragon King of the Eastern Sea.
events.summaryZh: 悟空操练群猴，却没有一件称手的兵器。
events.titleEn: A weapon from the Dragon King
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: After a drunken feast with six demon kings, Wukong dreamed that two summoners roped his soul and dragged it to the Land of Darkness.
events.summaryZh: 悟空回山后，又与牛魔王等六位妖王结为兄弟，天天宴饮。
events.titleEn: Striking out the Register of Death
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: As the Jade Emperor prepared to send troops, the Gold Star of Venus advised him to summon the monkey with a decree of amnesty and keep him in heaven under a title.
events.summaryZh: 玉帝看了两道表文，正要派兵捉拿，太白金星出班奏道：这猴子是天地育成之体，不如降一道招安圣旨，把他宣上天来，给他一个官职，拘束在此，若他受天命，以后再加升赏；若违天命，就地擒拿。
events.titleEn: Heaven's first office: Keeper of the Horses
events.titleZh: 天庭的第一份官职：弼马温
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Wukong raised a banner reading 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven'.

events.summaryEn: With nothing to do, the Great Sage wandered heaven befriending stars.
events.summaryZh: 大圣在天上无事可做，今天东游，明天西荡，和众星宿称兄道弟。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Freezing the fairies with an immobilising spell, the Great Sage flew to the Jade Pool, put the wine-makers to sleep with sleep-insects made from his hairs and drank himself senseless.
events.summaryZh: 大圣用定身法把七位仙女定在树下，驾云直奔瑶池。
events.titleEn: Stolen wine, stolen elixir and heaven's army

events.summaryEn: Guanyin recommended the Jade Emperor's nephew, the Illustrious Sage Erlang of Guanjiang.

events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Bound at the execution terrace, the Great Sage could not be hurt by sword, axe, fire or thunder: the peaches, wine and elixir had made his body adamantine.
events.summaryZh: 大圣被押到斩妖台，绑在降妖柱上。
events.titleEn: Fiery golden eyes in the Eight Trigrams furnace
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: Surrounded by Wang Lingguan and thirty-six thunder generals, the Great Sage fought them off with three heads, six arms and three staffs, until the Jade Emperor sent to the West for Rulai.
events.summaryZh: 王灵官和三十六员雷将把大圣团团围住，大圣变出三头六臂，把金箍棒幌一幌变成三根，六只手使开，打得雷将们近不了身。
events.uncertaintyNote: 神话地点不推测坐标。

events.summaryEn: To prove his journey he made a brush from a hair, wrote 'The Great Sage Equal to Heaven was here' on the middle pillar, and relieved himself at the foot of the first.
events.summaryZh: 大圣心想：我到了这里，回去跟如来做个凭证。
events.titleEn: Under the Mountain of Five Elements
events.uncertaintyNote: “五百年”的时间与后来唐僧解救的情节见于第八回之后，本篇只讲到被压为止。

versions.labelEn: Journey to the West, chapters 1–7 (long retelling)
versions.labelZh: 《西游记》第一至七回（长篇讲述）
versions.narrativeScope: 石猴出世、学艺、龙宫与地府、弼马温与齐天大圣、蟠桃会、二郎神、八卦炉与五行山
versions.rightsNote: 小说原文属公共领域；本站发布的是按回目顺序的独立白话讲述。

sections.bodyEn: Beyond the sea from the land of Aolai on the Eastern Continent stands the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit, and on its summit an immortal stone that had absorbed the essences of heaven and earth since the world began. One day it split open and released a stone egg; touched by the wind, the egg became a stone monkey. He bowed to the four quarters and beams of golden light shot from his eyes to the palace of the Pole Star. The Jade Emperor sent Thousand-Mile Eye and Wind-Following Ear to look; told it was only a monkey born of a stone, he declared such things unremarkable.
sections.bodyZh: 东胜神洲傲来国的海外，有一座花果山，山顶上立着一块仙石。这块石头高三丈六尺五寸，围圆二丈四尺，自开天辟地以来就吸收着天地的灵气和日月的精华，久而久之有了灵通。有一天，仙石崩裂，生出一枚石卵，石卵被风一吹，化成一只石猴，五官俱全，四肢皆备。石猴学会了爬和走，向四方拜了一拜，两只眼睛里射出两道金光，直冲天上的斗府。玉皇大帝被惊动，派千里眼和顺风耳打开南天门查看。两位神将回报说：那是花果山上仙石生出的一只猴子，如今他吃了东西、喝了水，金光就要渐渐消退了。玉帝听了说：下方之物，都是天地精华所生，不足为奇。——谁也没想到，这只猴子后来会把天宫闹得天翻地覆。
sections.headingEn: A stone gives birth to a monkey

sections.bodyEn: The monkey played among the other monkeys of the mountain. One hot summer they followed a stream up to a great waterfall and promised to make king whoever could pass through it unharmed. The stone monkey shut his eyes and leapt through. Behind the falling water lay an iron bridge and a cave-home furnished by nature with stone pots, beds and benches, and an inscription naming it the Water Curtain Cave of the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He led the monkeys inside, they bowed to him as the Handsome Monkey King, and he lived there freely for three or five hundred years.
sections.bodyZh: 石猴在山中和群猴一起玩耍，饿了吃草木果实，渴了喝山涧泉水。一个炎热的夏天，群猴在涧中洗澡，想去看看这股水从哪里来，便顺着山涧往上爬，一直找到一道大瀑布前。群猴拍手说：谁能钻进瀑布，找到源头又不伤身体，我们就拜他为王！石猴应声而出，闭上眼睛纵身一跳，竟穿过了瀑布。瀑布后面是一座铁板桥，桥那边是一处天造地设的洞府，石锅石灶、石床石凳一应俱全，石碣上刻着“花果山福地，水帘洞洞天”。石猴跳出来把群猴都领了进去，群猴依约向他跪拜，称他为“美猴王”。从此他去掉“石”字，自称“千岁大王”，在水帘洞里过了三五百年自在的日子。
sections.headingEn: King of the Water Curtain Cave

sections.bodyEn: One day at a feast the Monkey King suddenly wept. Though no human law ruled them and no beast threatened them, he said, one day they would grow old and the King of the Dead would claim them. An old gibbon told him that only buddhas, immortals and sages escape the wheel of rebirth. Overjoyed, the Monkey King resolved to find them and learn the way to live forever. The next morning the monkeys feasted him with fruit, and he set off alone across the ocean on a raft of pine logs with a bamboo pole.
sections.bodyZh: 有一天，美猴王和群猴正在饮宴，他忽然流下泪来。群猴问他为何烦恼，他说：我们现在虽然不受人间王法管束，也不怕飞禽走兽，可将来年老血衰，暗中有阎王老子管着，一旦死去，岂不白白在世上走了一遭？群猴听了，也都掩面悲啼。这时一只通背猿猴跳出来说：大王能想到这一层，就是道心开发了。五虫之中，只有三等名色不归阎王管——就是佛、仙与神圣，他们躲过轮回，与天地山川同寿。美猴王大喜，决心云游海角，去寻访这三等人物，学一个长生不老的法子。第二天，群猴摘来仙桃异果为他送行，他独自砍了松木扎成木筏，拿一根竹竿当篙，漂洋过海而去。

sections.bodyEn: The raft carried him to the Southern Continent, where for eight or nine years he learned human speech and dress but met only people chasing fame and profit. Crossing another ocean to the Western Continent, he heard a woodcutter singing an immortal's song and was directed to the Patriarch Subodhi of the Cave of the Slanting Moon and Three Stars on the Mountain of Mind. The patriarch, seeing a monkey (husun), gave him the surname Sun by removing the animal radical, and from the generation character wu named him Sun Wukong, 'Awakened to Emptiness'.
sections.bodyZh: 木筏被风吹到南赡部洲。美猴王上岸学人说话、穿人衣服，在市井里走了八九年，看到的都是为名为利奔忙的人，没有一个修仙的。他又扎筏渡过西洋大海，来到西牛贺洲。在一座高山上，他听见一个樵夫唱着仙家的歌，樵夫说歌是邻居一位神仙教的，那位神仙住在灵台方寸山，斜月三星洞，名叫须菩提祖师。美猴王找到洞门，等了半天，一个仙童开门迎他进去。祖师问他姓什么，他说“我无性，人若骂我，我也不恼”；又问籍贯，他说从东胜神洲来。祖师看他像个猢狲，便把“猢狲”去掉兽旁，给他姓“孙”，再按门中“广大智慧真如性海颖悟圆觉”十二字排到“悟”字，取名“孙悟空”。
sections.headingEn: The Cave of the Slanting Moon and Three Stars

sections.bodyEn: Wukong swept, fetched water and cut wood for six or seven years. When the patriarch offered him various arts, he refused each because none brought eternal life. Feigning anger, the patriarch struck him three times on the head, clasped his hands behind his back and shut the inner door. Wukong understood the riddle: come at the third watch, by the back door. That night the patriarch taught him the secret of long life, later the seventy-two earthly transformations to escape the calamities that strike immortals every five hundred years, and finally the somersault cloud that carries him 108,000 li in a single leap.
sections.bodyZh: 悟空在洞中扫地、挑水、砍柴，一住就是六七年。有一天祖师登坛讲道，问他想学什么：讲术、流、静、动各门，可以请仙问卜、读经念佛、打坐参禅、采阴补阳，悟空每听一门都先问一句“能长生吗”，听说不能，就一概不学。祖师假装发怒，跳下高台，拿戒尺在他头上打了三下，背着手走进里屋，关上了中门。众师兄都埋怨他，悟空却心里明白：打三下，是叫他三更时分去；背着手进去、关中门，是叫他从后门进来。当夜三更，他果然从后门溜进祖师卧房跪下。祖师见他领悟了哑谜，便把长生妙道的口诀传给他。三年之后，祖师又说修成的人每五百年要遭雷灾、火灾、风灾，便教他躲灾的七十二般地煞变化；后来又传他一个筋斗云，一翻就是十万八千里。
sections.headingEn: A secret lesson at the third watch

sections.bodyEn: One evening his fellow students begged to see his new powers, and Wukong turned himself into a pine tree to their loud applause. The patriarch, disturbed by the noise, rebuked him: an adept must not show off, for others will covet the art and trouble will follow. He sent Wukong away at once, forbidding him ever to name his teacher. Wukong somersaulted home, found that a Demon King of Confusion had seized his cave, plucked a handful of hairs that became hundreds of little monkeys, and killed the demon.
sections.bodyZh: 一天傍晚，众师兄围着悟空，要看他学来的变化。悟空经不住夸，捻着诀念动咒语，摇身一变，就变成一棵松树，众人齐声喝彩。吵闹声惊动了祖师，祖师把悟空叫来责备：修行之人不可在人前卖弄，别人见了要求你，你不教就会招来祸患。他命悟空立刻离开，并且叮嘱：此去无论惹出什么祸来，都不许说是我的徒弟，你只要说出半个字来，我就把你神魂贬在九幽之处。悟空含泪拜别，一个筋斗回到花果山。他得知一个混世魔王趁他不在，霸占了水帘洞、掳走了小猴，便找上门去，拔一把毫毛变出几百个小猴，把魔王打死，夺回了洞府。

sections.bodyEn: Needing a weapon, Wukong dived to the Crystal Palace of Ao Guang, Dragon King of the Eastern Sea. A broadsword, a nine-pronged fork of 3,600 pounds and a halberd of 7,200 pounds were all too light. The Dragon Queen suggested the divine iron that had fixed the depth of the Milky Way, which had lately been glowing. It was a pillar inscribed 'Compliant Golden-Hooped Rod, weight 13,500 pounds', and it shrank at his command until it was the size of an embroidery needle, which he kept behind his ear. He then bullied the dragon kings of the four seas into giving him cloud-walking shoes, golden mail and a phoenix-feather cap.
sections.bodyZh: 悟空操练群猴，却没有一件称手的兵器。他得知花果山下的铁板桥直通东海龙宫，便捻着闭水诀钻进水里，向东海龙王敖广讨兵器。龙王先后拿出一把大刀、一柄重三千六百斤的九股叉、一杆重七千二百斤的方天画戟，悟空都嫌太轻。龙婆、龙女出主意说：海藏里那块天河定底的神珍铁，这几天霞光艳艳，莫非是该出世遇此圣人？悟空过去一看，是一根斗来粗、二丈多长的铁柱，两头是金箍，中间刻着“如意金箍棒，重一万三千五百斤”。他说声“再短细些”，铁棒就随心变小，最后成了绣花针大小，藏进耳朵里。他又逼着四海龙王凑出藕丝步云履、锁子黄金甲和凤翅紫金冠，才心满意足地回山。
sections.headingEn: A weapon from the Dragon King

sections.bodyEn: After a drunken feast with six demon kings, Wukong dreamed that two summoners roped his soul and dragged it to the Land of Darkness. Furious — had he not passed beyond the Three Realms? — he beat them to pulp with his staff and stormed the palace of the Ten Kings of the Underworld. There he found his own entry, 'Sun Wukong, stone monkey born of heaven, allotted 342 years, to die a good death', and with a brush struck out his name and those of all monkeys. When he woke, the Dragon King and the King Qinguang of the underworld each sent complaints to heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 悟空回山后，又与牛魔王等六位妖王结为兄弟，天天宴饮。一天他喝醉了，在松树下睡着，梦见两个人拿着勾魂的牌子，用绳子套住他的魂魄，一直拉到幽冥界。悟空看见城上写着“幽冥界”，大怒道：我老孙早已超出三界之外，跳出五行之中，凭什么来勾我？他从耳中掏出金箍棒，把两个勾死人打成肉酱，一路打进森罗殿。十殿阎王只好叫判官拿出生死簿给他看。悟空翻到“魂字一千三百五十号”，上面写着“孙悟空，天产石猴，该寿三百四十二岁，善终”。他索性拿笔把自己和猴类的名字一概勾掉，扔下簿子打出幽冥界。醒来后，东海龙王和地府的秦广王先后上表天庭，状告这只妖猴。
sections.headingEn: Striking out the Register of Death

sections.bodyEn: As the Jade Emperor prepared to send troops, the Gold Star of Venus advised him to summon the monkey with a decree of amnesty and keep him in heaven under a title. Wukong happily accepted and was appointed Keeper of the Heavenly Horses, tending them so well that they grew sleek within a fortnight. At a banquet he learned that the post had no rank at all. Enraged at having been tricked into grooming horses, he overturned his desk, fought his way out through the Southern Gate and returned home, where a demon king urged him to proclaim himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 玉帝看了两道表文，正要派兵捉拿，太白金星出班奏道：这猴子是天地育成之体，不如降一道招安圣旨，把他宣上天来，给他一个官职，拘束在此，若他受天命，以后再加升赏；若违天命，就地擒拿。玉帝准奏。悟空欢喜上天，被封为御马监的弼马温。他尽心尽力，半个月里把天马养得肉肥膘满。一天同僚设宴，他问起弼马温是几品官，众人说：这官没有品从，叫作“未入流”，养得好不过是一声“好”，养瘦了还要受罚。悟空听了大怒：老孙在花果山称王称祖，怎么骗我来替他养马！他推倒公案，掣出铁棒，一路打出南天门，回到花果山。独角鬼王献上赭黄袍，劝他索性做个“齐天大圣”。
sections.headingEn: Heaven's first office: Keeper of the Horses
sections.headingZh: 天庭的第一份官职：弼马温

sections.bodyEn: Wukong raised a banner reading 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven'. The Jade Emperor sent Heavenly King Li and his son Nezha with heaven's soldiers. The vanguard, the Mighty Spirit, had his axe-handle snapped by one blow; Nezha took three heads and six arms, but Wukong did the same, sent a hair-double to fight, and struck Nezha from behind. Venus advised granting the empty title Great Sage Equal to Heaven, with no salary, to quiet the monkey's heart. A mansion was built for him beside the Peach Garden, complete with Offices of Peace and Serenity, and Wukong settled happily in heaven.
sections.bodyZh: 悟空在洞门外竖起一面大旗，上书“齐天大圣”四个大字。玉帝派托塔李天王和哪吒三太子带领天兵下界捉拿。先锋巨灵神挥着宣花斧上阵，被悟空一棒打断斧柄，败回营中。哪吒变出三头六臂，持六般兵器来战，悟空也变三头六臂，又拔一根毫毛变作本相迎敌，真身绕到背后，一棒打中哪吒的左臂，哪吒负痛败走。李天王只好收兵回奏。太白金星又出主意：不如就封他个空衔“齐天大圣”，有官无禄，养在天地之间，收他的邪心。玉帝依从，在蟠桃园右首给他盖了一座齐天大圣府，府里还设了安静司、宁神司两个衙门。悟空这才欢天喜地，在天上住了下来。

sections.bodyEn: With nothing to do, the Great Sage wandered heaven befriending stars. To keep him occupied the Jade Emperor put him in charge of the Garden of Immortal Peaches, whose 3,600 trees ripened every three, six and nine thousand years, granting immortality, eternal youth and a life as long as heaven and earth. Secretly delighted, he sent his attendants away and gorged on the ripest fruit. When seven fairy maidens came to pick peaches for the Queen Mother's Peach Banquet, they woke him from a nap in the treetops — and he learned that he had not been invited.
sections.bodyZh: 大圣在天上无事可做，今天东游，明天西荡，和众星宿称兄道弟。许旌阳真人担心他闲中生事，玉帝便派他去管理蟠桃园。土地告诉他：园里共有三千六百株桃树——前面一千二百株，三千年一熟，人吃了成仙了道；中间一千二百株，六千年一熟，人吃了霞举飞升、长生不老；后面一千二百株，九千年一熟，人吃了与天地齐寿、日月同庚。大圣听了暗暗高兴，从此常常支开土地和力士，自己脱下冠服爬上大树，拣那熟透的大桃子吃个饱。有一天，王母娘娘要开蟠桃盛会，派七位仙女提着花篮来园中摘桃。大圣正变成二寸长的小人在树梢上睡觉，被惊醒后问仙女都请了谁，仙女一一说来，却没有他。

sections.bodyEn: Freezing the fairies with an immobilising spell, the Great Sage flew to the Jade Pool, put the wine-makers to sleep with sleep-insects made from his hairs and drank himself senseless. Staggering the wrong way, he wandered into Laozi's Tushita Palace and ate the five gourds of finished elixir pills as if they were roasted beans. Sobering in alarm, he fled home. The Jade Emperor sent the Four Heavenly Kings, Heavenly King Li, Nezha, the twenty-eight lunar mansions and the nine planets with a hundred thousand soldiers and eighteen nets around the mountain, yet the Great Sage held them off until nightfall.
sections.bodyZh: 大圣用定身法把七位仙女定在树下，驾云直奔瑶池。宴席已经摆好，他拔毫毛变出瞌睡虫，叫造酒的力士都睡着了，自己端起玉液琼浆喝了个酩酊大醉。醉醺醺的他走错了路，闯进太上老君的兜率宫，宫中无人，只见丹房里摆着五个葫芦，装满炼好的金丹。他想：这是仙家至宝，我且尝尝。于是把葫芦里的金丹倒出来，像吃炒豆一样全吃了。酒醒之后，他知道闯了大祸，连忙逃出西天门，回到花果山。玉帝大怒，派四大天王、李天王、哪吒，率领二十八宿、九曜星官、十二元辰等十万天兵，布下十八架天罗地网围住花果山。大圣带着群猴迎战，一连打败九曜星和四大天王，到天黑也没有被捉住。
sections.headingEn: Stolen wine, stolen elixir and heaven's army

sections.bodyEn: Guanyin recommended the Jade Emperor's nephew, the Illustrious Sage Erlang of Guanjiang. With his six sworn brothers and his celestial hound, Erlang fought the Great Sage for over three hundred rounds. When the monkeys scattered, the Great Sage fled through transformation after transformation — sparrow, cormorant, fish, water snake, bustard — and Erlang matched each as hawk, crane, osprey and grey crane. Disguised as a temple, the monkey could not hide his tail and stood it up behind as a flagpole, which gave him away. At last Laozi dropped his Diamond Snare on his head, the hound bit his leg, and he was seized.
sections.bodyZh: 观音菩萨赴蟠桃会，听说此事，先派徒弟惠岸行者下界交战，也败了回来。观音便向玉帝推荐玉帝的外甥——住在灌江口的显圣二郎真君。二郎神带着梅山六兄弟和哮天犬来到花果山，和大圣大战三百余回合，不分胜负，各自变成万丈高的法身相斗。猴群溃散，大圣心慌，收了法相变成一只麻雀飞上树梢；二郎就变成饿鹰去扑他。大圣变成大鹚老冲天飞去，二郎变成海鹤追赶；他变鱼钻进水里，二郎变鱼鹰候着；他变水蛇，二郎变灰鹤；他变成一只低贱的花鸨，二郎不屑追，用弹弓把他打落。大圣滚到山崖下又变成一座土地庙，嘴变庙门，牙变门扇，舌头变菩萨，尾巴没处放，竖在后面变成一根旗杆，被二郎一眼识破。最后太上老君在云端丢下金刚琢，正打在大圣头上，哮天犬扑上来咬住他的腿，大圣才被众神按倒擒住。

sections.bodyEn: Bound at the execution terrace, the Great Sage could not be hurt by sword, axe, fire or thunder: the peaches, wine and elixir had made his body adamantine. Laozi had him placed in his Eight Trigrams furnace to be refined for forty-nine days. Hiding under the trigram of wind, where there is no fire, he was only smoked — which reddened his eyes into 'fiery golden eyes'. When the furnace was opened he sprang out, kicked it over so that its burning bricks fell to earth, and fought his way to the Hall of Divine Mists, where only the officer Wang Lingguan stood against him.
sections.bodyZh: 大圣被押到斩妖台，绑在降妖柱上。天兵刀砍斧剁、枪刺剑刳，火部众神放火烧、雷部众神用雷劈，竟伤不了他一根毫毛。太上老君说：这猴子吃了蟠桃、喝了御酒，又盗吃了我的金丹，炼成了金刚之躯。不如交给我，放进八卦炉里，用文武火锻炼，炼出我的丹来，他的身体自然化为灰烬。大圣被推进八卦炉，他钻进巽宫位下——巽是风，有风就没有火，只是被烟熏红了眼睛，从此有了一双“火眼金睛”。四十九天后，老君开炉取丹，大圣忽地跳了出来，一脚蹬倒八卦炉，炉砖带着火掉落凡间。他掏出金箍棒，从兜率宫一路打到灵霄殿外，九曜星闭门闭户，四天王无影无踪，只有王灵官举着金鞭拦住了他。
sections.headingEn: Fiery golden eyes in the Eight Trigrams furnace

sections.bodyEn: Surrounded by Wang Lingguan and thirty-six thunder generals, the Great Sage fought them off with three heads, six arms and three staffs, until the Jade Emperor sent to the West for Rulai. Asked what right he had to the throne, the Great Sage replied that emperors take turns — next year it would be his. Rulai offered a wager: if he could somersault out of Rulai's right palm, the Jade Emperor would yield heaven; if not, he must return below. Scoffing that his somersault covered 108,000 li, the Great Sage leapt — and came to five flesh-pink pillars he took to be the edge of the sky.
sections.bodyZh: 王灵官和三十六员雷将把大圣团团围住，大圣变出三头六臂，把金箍棒幌一幌变成三根，六只手使开，打得雷将们近不了身。玉帝只好派游弈灵官和翊圣真君到西方去请如来佛祖。如来来到灵霄殿外，叫雷将停手，问大圣：你有什么本事，敢夺玉帝的尊位？大圣说：“皇帝轮流做，明年到我家”，只要玉帝把天宫让给他就罢了。如来笑道：我和你打个赌——你若一个筋斗翻得出我的右手掌，就算你赢，请玉帝到西方居住，天宫让给你；若翻不出去，你就回下界做妖，再修几劫来争。大圣暗笑：我一个筋斗十万八千里，他的手掌不满一尺，怎么跳不出去？他跳上佛掌，一个筋斗云不见踪影，只见天边立着五根肉红柱子，便以为到了天的尽头。

sections.bodyEn: To prove his journey he made a brush from a hair, wrote 'The Great Sage Equal to Heaven was here' on the middle pillar, and relieved himself at the foot of the first. Somersaulting back, he demanded the throne. Rulai showed him the words written on his own middle finger and the smell of monkey urine at the base of his thumb. Before the monkey could leap again, Rulai pushed him out of the Western Gate and turned his five fingers into the five joined peaks of Metal, Wood, Water, Fire and Earth — the Mountain of Five Elements — sealed with a golden six-syllable charm. The local god was to feed him iron pellets and molten copper until, five hundred years later, someone would come to free him.
sections.bodyZh: 大圣心想：我到了这里，回去跟如来做个凭证。他拔一根毫毛变出一支浓墨双毫笔，在中间那根柱子上写下一行大字：“齐天大圣到此一游”。写完收了毫毛，又不庄重地在第一根柱子下撒了一泡猴尿，然后翻转筋斗回到原处，对如来说：我已经去了又回来了，你叫玉帝让出天宫吧！如来骂道：你这尿精猴子，你正好不曾离开我的手掌！你低头看看。大圣一看，如来右手中指上写着“齐天大圣到此一游”，大拇指根下还有一股猴尿的臊气。他大吃一惊，正要再跳，被如来翻掌一扑，推出西天门外，五根手指化作金、木、水、火、土五座相连的大山，叫作“五行山”，把他压在山下。众神在天宫摆了“安天大会”答谢如来。如来又取出写着“唵、嘛、呢、叭、咪、吽”六个金字的帖子，贴在山顶，并嘱咐当地的土地神：他饿了就给他吃铁丸子，渴了就给他喝熔化的铜汁。等他的灾难满了，自然会有人来救他。——这一压，就是五百年。
sections.headingEn: Under the Mountain of Five Elements
sections.uncertaintyNote: “五百年”的时间与后来唐僧解救的情节见于第八回之后，本篇只讲到被压为止。

stories.canonicalTitle: Nezha conquers the sea — the lotus rebirth in Investiture of the Gods
stories.editorialNote: 明代小说属于后世文学接受层；按回目顺序独立讲述，现代影视改编不合并。
stories.summaryEn: Lady Yin, wife of Li Jing of Chentang Pass, carries her child for three years and six months and gives birth to a ball of flesh, from which springs Nezha wearing a golden ring and a red sash. At seven he shakes the Dragon King's palace while bathing, kills a patrolling yaksha and the dragon prince Ao Bing, beats the Dragon King at the gate of heaven and accidentally kills an immortal's disciple. When the dragon kings seize his parents, he returns his flesh and bones to them; his teacher Taiyi rebuilds him from lotus, and he hunts his father until Li Jing receives a golden pagoda.
stories.summaryZh: 陈塘关总兵李靖的夫人怀胎三年六个月，生下一个肉球，球里跳出戴着乾坤圈、裹着混天绫的哪吒。七岁那年，他在九湾河洗澡震动东海龙宫，打死夜叉和龙王三太子敖丙；又在宝德门外痛打东海龙王，误射死石矶娘娘的徒弟。四海龙王捉走他的父母，哪吒剖腹剜肠、剔骨还父、割肉还母。太乙真人用莲花为他重造身体，哪吒追杀李靖，直到燃灯道人赐下玲珑宝塔。
stories.titleZh: 哪吒闹海：《封神演义》里的莲花化身

claims.statement: Li Jing's wife Lady Yin carries her third child for three years and six months and dreams of a Daoist handing her a 'unicorn child'.
Li Jing cuts open the ball of flesh and a glowing boy springs out wearing a golden ring on his arm and a red silk sash.
Taiyi Zhenren of the Golden Light Cave names the child Nezha and takes him as his disciple.
At seven, bathing in the Nine Bends River, Nezha swishes his sash in the water and shakes the Dragon King's Crystal Palace.
Nezha kills the patrolling yaksha Li Gen with his ring and then the Dragon King's third son Ao Bing, whose sinew he pulls out.
Ao Guang comes to Chentang Pass in human form, finds Nezha braiding his son's sinew, and vows to accuse Li Jing and Nezha before the Jade Emperor.
Made invisible by Taiyi's charm, Nezha ambushes Ao Guang outside the Gate of Treasured Virtue, tears off his scales and carries him home as a little green snake.
Nezha draws the Yellow Emperor's Universe Bow and his arrow kills the Green Cloud boy, disciple of Lady Shiji.
Taiyi Zhenren traps Lady Shiji under his Nine-Dragon Divine Fire Cover and burns her back into her original form, a stone.
To free his parents from the four dragon kings, Nezha cuts open his body and returns his flesh and bones to his parents, and dies.
Finding pilgrims at the shrine his wife secretly built for Nezha on Cuiping Mountain, Li Jing smashes the statue and burns the shrine.
Taiyi Zhenren rebuilds Nezha's body from lotus stems and leaves with an elixir pill and gives him the fire-tipped spear and the wind-and-fire wheels.
Pursued by the reborn Nezha, Li Jing receives the golden pagoda from Randeng Daoren, which forces Nezha to acknowledge him and gives him the title Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King.

events.summaryEn: In the last years of the Shang, Li Jing, commander of Chentang Pass, had once studied the arts of the Five Elements with an immortal before coming down the mountain to serve King Zhou.

events.summaryZh: 两个侍女慌慌张张跑来报告：夫人生下了一个妖精！

events.summaryEn: At seven years old and six feet tall, Nezha went outside the pass one hot day in the fifth month with a servant.
events.summaryZh: 光阴似箭，哪吒长到七岁，身高六尺。

events.summaryZh: 龙王派巡海夜叉李艮去看看出了什么事。
events.titleEn: The yaksha and the third prince

events.summaryEn: Ao Guang, grieving for his son, came to Chentang Pass in the form of a scholar and demanded the killer.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒回到家里，若无其事。

events.summaryEn: Nezha travelled underground to his teacher.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒借土遁到乾元山，向太乙真人说明经过。
events.titleEn: Beating the Dragon King at the Gate of Treasured Virtue

events.summaryZh: 龙王放回后，怀恨而去。
events.titleEn: An arrow kills the Green Cloud boy

events.summaryEn: At Skull Mountain Nezha fought Lady Shiji, who caught his ring and sash with her eight-trigram cloud-light kerchief.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒来到骷髅山，和石矶娘娘一言不合就动起手来。

events.summaryEn: Ao Guang had gathered the dragon kings of the southern, western and northern seas, and with the Jade Emperor's warrant they seized Li Jing and Lady Yin.
events.summaryZh: 原来东海龙王敖光不甘心，约了南海、西海、北海三位龙王，一起上奏玉帝。
events.titleEn: Returning his bones to his father and his flesh to his mother

events.summaryEn: Nezha's soul drifted to his teacher, who told him to appear in his mother's dreams and ask for a shrine on Cuiping Mountain, forty li from the pass; after three years of incense he could return to the world.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒的魂魄飘飘荡荡，来到乾元山。

events.summaryEn: Taiyi had his servant fetch two lotus flowers and three lotus leaves from the Five-Lotus Pond.
events.summaryZh: 太乙真人叫金霞童子到五莲池摘两枝莲花、三片荷叶来。

events.summaryEn: Riding his wind-and-fire wheels with the fire-tipped spear, Nezha stormed Chentang Pass in pursuit of his father.
events.summaryZh: 哪吒踏着风火轮，提着火尖枪，直奔陈塘关找李靖算账。
events.titleEn: Father against son, and the golden pagoda
